title: Console Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Console Settings

This page covers settings that manage access and behavior for the Console UI.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Browser settings

The following settings control behavior for the embedded Console UI.

Enable embedded console

Optional

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER
This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Specify off to disable the embedded Console UI.

Animation

Optional

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_LOGIN_ANIMATION

Specify off to disable the animated login screen for the Console UI. Defaults to on.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Browser redirect

Optional

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_REDIRECT

Specify whether requests from a web browser automatically redirect to the Console address. Defaults to true.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Browser redirect URL

Optional

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL

Specify the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) the Console UI listens for incoming connections on.

If you want to host the Console UI exclusively from a reverse-proxy service, you must specify the hostname managed by that service.

For example, consider a reverse proxy configured to route https://example.net/hypervault/ to the Console UI. You must set this environment variable to match that hostname for the Console to both listen and respond to requests using that hostname.

If you omit this variable, the Console listens and responds to all IP addresses or hostnames associated to the host machine on which the Object Store runs.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Session duration

Optional

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_SESSION_DURATION

Specify the duration of a browser session for working with the Console UI.

HyperVault supports the following units of time measurement:

  • s - seconds, “60s”
  • m - minutes, “60m”
  • h - hours, “24h”
  • d - days, “7d”

Defaults to 12h.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Log query URL

Optional

HYPERVAULT_LOG_QUERY_URL

Specify the URL of a PostgreSQL service to which HyperVault writes Audit logs. The embedded Console UI provides a Log Search tool that allows querying the PostgreSQL service for collected logs.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Content security policy

Optional

Configure Console UI to generate a Content-Security-Policy header in HTTP responses. Defaults to default-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline';

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY

export HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY="default-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline';"

browser csp_policy

mc admin config set browser \
   csp_policy="default-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline';" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Strict transport security

Optional

Configure Console UI to generate a Strict-Transport-Security header in HTTP responses.

To generate the header, you must set a duration using either HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_HSTS_SECONDS or hsts_seconds. Other HSTS settings are optional.

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_HSTS_SECONDS

The max_age the configured policy remains in effect, in seconds. Defaults to 0, disabled. You must configure a non-zero duration to enable the Strict-Transport-Security header.

export HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_HSTS_SECONDS=31536000

browser hsts_seconds

The max_age the configured policy remains in effect, in seconds. Defaults to 0, disabled. You must configure a non-zero duration to enable the Strict-Transport-Security header.

mc admin config set browser \
   hsts_seconds="31536000" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUB_DOMAINS

Set to on to also apply the configured HSTS policy to all Console UI subdomains. Defaults to off.

export HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUB_DOMAINS="on"

browser hsts_include_subdomains

Set to on to also apply the configured HSTS policy to all Console UI subdomains. Defaults to off.

mc admin config set browser \
   hsts_include_subdomains="on" \
   hsts_seconds="31536000" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_HSTS_PRELOAD

Set to on to direct the client browser to add the Console UI domain to its HSTS preload list. Defaults to off.

export HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_HSTS_PRELOAD="on"

browser hsts_preload

Set to on to direct the client browser to add the Console UI domain to its HSTS preload list. Defaults to off.

mc admin config set browser \
   hsts_preload="on" \
   hsts_seconds="31536000" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Examples

The following examples show the rendered header for the given configuration settings. The equivalent environment variables generate the same result. All examples use a value of 31536000, which is the number of seconds in a calendar year (365 days).

hsts_seconds

mc admin config set ALIAS browser hsts_seconds=31536000

Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000

hsts_include_subdomains

mc admin config set ALIAS browser hsts_seconds=31536000 hsts_include_subdomains=on

Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

hsts_preload

mc admin config set ALIAS browser hsts_seconds=31536000 hsts_include_subdomains=on hsts_preload=on

Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

Referrer policy

Optional

Configure Console UI to generate a Referrer-Policy header in HTTP responses. Defaults to strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_REFERRER_POLICY

export HYPERVAULT_BROWSER_REFERRER_POLICY="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

browser referrer_policy

mc admin config set browser \
   referrer_policy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Prometheus settings

The following settings manage how HyperVault interacts with your Prometheus service.

Prometheus URL

Optional

HYPERVAULT_PROMETHEUS_URL

Specify the URL for a Prometheus service configured to scrape HyperVault metrics.

The Console UI populates the Dashboard with cluster metrics using the hypervault-job Prometheus scraping job.

If you are using a standalone Console UI process, this variable corresponds with CONSOLE_PROMETHEUS_URL.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Prometheus job ID

Optional

HYPERVAULT_PROMETHEUS_JOB_ID

Specify the custom Prometheus job ID used for scraping HyperVault metrics.

HyperVault defaults to hypervault-job.

If you are using a standalone Console UI process, this variable corresponds with CONSOLE_PROMETHEUS_JOB_ID.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

Prometheus auth token

Optional

HYPERVAULT_PROMETHEUS_AUTH_TOKEN

Specify the basic auth token the Console should use to connect to a Prometheus service.

For example, a basic auth token you might use could resemble the following:

eyJhbGciOiJIUzUxMiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJwcm9tZXRoZXVzIiwic3ViIjoibWluaW8iLCJleHAiOjQ4NTAwMzg0MDJ9.GZCKR3d0FH2TCvNHSd39HaVfSuQVVV0s8glICBDmhT51V6CQ_hw8gTYlKHJmcpR8aHkqiJwCqcYJhaMmqwe00XY

If you are using a standalone Console UI process, this variable corresponds with CONSOLE_PROMETHEUS_AUTH_TOKEN.

This setting does not have a configuration variable setting. Use the Environment Variable instead.

title: Core Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Core Settings

This page covers settings that control core behavior of the HyperVault process.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Server CLI options

HYPERVAULT_OPTS

Optional

Set a string of parameters to use when starting the HyperVault Server. This environment variable only applies for systems using the default systemd service installed using first-party DEB or RPM packages. See Install HyperVault on Linux for more information.

Use the /etc/default/hypervault file and create an environment variable HYPERVAULT_OPTS for specifying parameters to append to the hypervault process started with systemctl service start hypervault:

# Editing /etc/default/hypervault

HYPERVAULT_OPTS=' --console-address=":9001" --ftp="address=:8021" --ftp="passive-port-range=30000-40000" '

If running hypervault on the command line or using a custom systemd unit file that omits HYPERVAULT_OPTS, use HYPERVAULT_ARGS instead:

export HYPERVAULT_ARGS=' --console-address=":9001" --ftp="address=:8021" --ftp="passive-port-range=30000-40000" '

hypervault server ...

# The above is equivalent to running the following:
# hypervault server --console-address=":9001" \
#              --ftp="address=:8021"     \
#              --ftp="passive-port-range=30000-40000"
There is no configuration setting for this variable, as these settings apply at server startup.

HyperVault license

HYPERVAULT_LICENSE

Path to the hypervault.license file downloaded from SUBNET.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Storage volumes

HYPERVAULT_VOLUMES

The directories or drives the hypervault server process uses as the storage backend.

Functionally equivalent to setting hypervault server DIRECTORIES. Use this value when configuring HyperVault to run using an environment file.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Address

HYPERVAULT_ADDRESS

Specifies the hostname and port on which the server listens for incoming connections. Equivalent to the following:

  • CLI parameter hypervault server --address
  • Configuration file setting address

The order of precedence is as follows:

  1. Configuration file setting
  2. Environment variable
  3. CLI parameter

Use this value when configuring HyperVault to run using an environment file.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Console Address

HYPERVAULT_CONSOLE_ADDRESS

Specifies the hostname and port on which the web console listens for incoming connections. Equivalent to the following:

  • CLI parameter hypervault server --console-address
  • Configuration file setting console-address

The order of precedence is as follows:

  1. Configuration file setting
  2. Environment variable
  3. CLI parameter

Use this value when configuring HyperVault to run using an environment file.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Environment variable file path

HYPERVAULT_CONFIG_ENV_FILE

Specifies the full path to the file the Object Store process uses for loading environment variables.

For systemd-managed files, set this value to the path of the environment file (/etc/default/hypervault) to direct HyperVault to reload changes to that file when using mc admin service restart to restart the deployment.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Workers for expiration

HYPERVAULT_ILM_EXPIRY_WORKERS

Specifies the number of workers to make available to expire objects configured with ILM rules for expiration. When not set, HyperVault defaults to using up to half of the available processing cores available.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Domain

HYPERVAULT_DOMAIN

Enables Virtual Host-style requests to the HyperVault deployment. Set the value to the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) for HyperVault to accept incoming virtual host requests.

Omitting this setting directs HyperVault to only accept the default path-style requests.

For example, consider a HyperVault deployment with an assigned FQDN of hypervault.example.net.

  • With path-style lookups, applications can access the bucket using its full path as hypervault.example.net/mybucket.
  • With virtual-host lookups, application can access the bucket as a virtual host as mybucket.hypervault.example.net/.

To configure more than one domain, set HYPERVAULT_DOMAIN to a comma-separated list of FQDNs, such as hypervault.example.net,s3.example.net.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Configure virtual-host-style requests

Setting HYPERVAULT_DOMAIN alone is not sufficient. Because each bucket is addressed as a subdomain of the configured domain (mybucket.hypervault.example.net), the surrounding DNS and TLS configuration must also resolve and secure those subdomains.

To support virtual-host-style addressing for a domain such as hypervault.example.net:

  1. Set HYPERVAULT_DOMAIN on every HyperVault node.

    Set the environment variable to the domain (or comma-separated list of domains) on each server in the deployment and restart the nodes so the setting takes effect.

    export HYPERVAULT_DOMAIN=hypervault.example.net

  2. Create a wildcard DNS record.

    Add a wildcard DNS entry that resolves *.hypervault.example.net to the deployment (or to the load balancer in front of it), in addition to the existing record for the bare hypervault.example.net domain. Without the wildcard record, requests to mybucket.hypervault.example.net cannot reach the deployment.

  3. Use a TLS certificate that covers the wildcard domain.

    Virtual-host-style requests are sent to bucket subdomains, so the TLS certificate presented by HyperVault (or by the load balancer terminating TLS) must include both the bare domain and the wildcard domain in its Subject Alternative Name (SAN) list:

    • hypervault.example.net
    • *.hypervault.example.net

    A certificate issued only for hypervault.example.net causes TLS hostname-verification errors when clients connect to mybucket.hypervault.example.net. Wildcard certificates match only a single label, so a nested path such as mybucket.sub.hypervault.example.net is not covered.

  4. Configure any load balancer or proxy to forward the wildcard host.

    If a load balancer or reverse proxy sits in front of the deployment, configure it to route *.hypervault.example.net to the HyperVault nodes and to preserve the original Host header so HyperVault can resolve the bucket from the request.

After completing these steps, applications can address buckets either by path (hypervault.example.net/mybucket) or as a virtual host (mybucket.hypervault.example.net).

Scanner speed

HYPERVAULT_SCANNER_SPEED

scanner speed

Manage the maximum wait period for the scanner when balancing HyperVault read/write performance to scanner processes.

HyperVault utilizes the scanner for bucket replication, site replication, lifecycle management, and healing tasks.

Valid values include:

Setting Description
fastest Removes scanner wait on read/write latency, allowing the scanner to operate at full-speed and IOPS consumption.
This setting may result in reduced read and write performance.
fast Sets a short scanner wait time on read/write latency, allowing the scanner to operate at a higher speed and IOPS consumption.
This setting may result in reduced read and write performance.
default Sets a moderate scanner wait time on read/write latency, allowing the scanner to operate at a balanced speed and IOPS consumption.
This setting seeks to maintain read and write performance while allowing ongoing scanner activity.
slow Sets a medium scanner wait time on read/write latency, where the scanner operates at a reduced speed and IOPS consumption.
This setting allows better read and write performance while reducing scanner performance.

May impact scanner-dependent features, such as lifecycle management and replication.
slowest Sets a large scanner wait time on read/write latency, where the scanner operates at a substantially lower speed and IOPS consumption.
This setting prioritizes read and write operations at the potential cost of scanner operations.

May impact scanner-dependent features, such as lifecycle management and replication.

Data compression

The following section documents settings for enabling data compression for objects. See Data Compression for tutorials on using these configuration settings.

All of the settings in this section fall under the compression top-level key.

Enable compression

HYPERVAULT_COMPRESSION_ENABLE
compression enable

Optional

Set to on to enable data compression for new objects. Defaults to off.

Enabling or disabling data compression does not change existing objects.

Allow encryption

HYPERVAULT_COMPRESSION_ALLOW_ENCRYPTION
compression allow_encryption

Optional

Set to on to encrypt objects after compressing them. Defaults to off.

Compression extensions

HYPERVAULT_COMPRESSION_EXTENSIONS
compression extensions

Optional

Comma-separated list of the file extensions to compress. Setting a new list of file extensions replaces the previously configured list. Defaults to ".txt, .log, .csv, .json, .tar, .xml, .bin".

Specify "*" to direct HyperVault to compress all supported file types.

HyperVault does not support compressing file types on the Excluded File Types list, even if explicitly specified in this argument.

Compression MIME types

HYPERVAULT_COMPRESSION_MIME_TYPES
compression mime_types

Optional

Comma-separated list of the MIME types to compress. Setting a new list of types replaces the previously configured list. Defaults to "text/*, application/json, application/xml, binary/octet-stream".

Comments

This setting does not have an environment variable option. Use the configuration setting instead.
compression comment

Optional

Specify a comment to associate with the data compression configuration.

Erasure set drive count

HYPERVAULT_ERASURE_SET_DRIVE_COUNT

Optional

The erasure set size to apply for all drives in a given server pool.

By default, HyperVault limits erasure set sizes to 16 drives for optimal performance and network efficiency. For deployments requiring larger set sizes, you can set this variable to a value between 17 and 32 starting with HyperVault Server RELEASE.2026-02-02T23-40-11Z.

  • Default: Maximum 16 drives per set (automatic detection)
  • Configurable range: 17-32 drives per set

For example, with HYPERVAULT_ERASURE_SET_DRIVE_COUNT=32 and 128 total drives, HyperVault creates 4 sets with 32 drives each. Without this variable, the same configuration creates 8 sets with 16 drives each.

If you set this value, you must do so before you initialize the cluster. The selected stripe size is immutable after the cluster has been initialized and affects any future server pools added to the cluster.

HyperVault SUBNET users should log in and open an issue to discuss stripe size settings prior to implementing them in any environment.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.
Changes to stripe size have significant impact to deployment functionality, availability, performance, and behavior. HyperVault’s stripe selection algorithms set appropriate defaults for the majority of workloads. Consult with HyperVault engineering before changing the stripe size from the default.

Maximum drive usage

HYPERVAULT_DRIVE_MAX_USAGE_PCT
drive max_usage_pct

Optional

The maximum percentage of drive capacity that can be used before HyperVault returns HTTP 507 (Insufficient Storage) errors for new write operations.

Specify a value between 50 and 99. Defaults to 99.

When drive usage exceeds this threshold, the following operations return 507 errors:

  • Single object uploads (PUT)
  • Multipart uploads
  • Copy operations
  • Append operations

Other operations continue normally, including:

  • Healing
  • Decommissioning
  • Rebalancing
  • Listing operations
  • Metadata updates

This setting helps prevent drives from becoming completely full, which can cause operational issues.

Requires HyperVault Server RELEASE.2026-02-02T23-40-11Z or later.

Drive operation timeout

HYPERVAULT_DRIVE_MAX_TIMEOUT
drive max_timeout

Optional

The maximum time to wait for a single drive operation to complete. Defaults to 30s.

Specify a Go duration string (for example, 30s, 1m, 2m30s). The minimum duration allowed is 1s.

Increase this value for deployments with slower storage (such as HDDs) or high-latency network-attached storage. Decrease this value to fail faster on unresponsive drives.

Drive pre-allocation

HYPERVAULT_DRIVE_PREALLOCATE
drive preallocate

Optional

Enables file pre-allocation using posix_fallocate when writing objects. Defaults to off.

Set to on to pre-allocate disk space before writing data. This can reduce fragmentation on some filesystems and improve write performance for large objects.

Maximum object versions

HYPERVAULT_API_OBJECT_MAX_VERSIONS
api object_max_versions

Optional

Defines the default maximum versions to allow per object.

By default, HyperVault allows up to the maximum value of an Int64 versions per object, or over 9.2 quintillion.

Arbitrarily high versions per objects may cause performance degradation on some operations, such as LIST. This is especially true on systems running budget hardware or spinning drives (HDD). Applications or workloads which produce thousands or more versions per object may require design or architecture review to mitigate potential performance degradations.

Setting a limit of no more than 100 should provide enough versions for most typical use cases.

Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)

Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) is a browser security mechanism that controls which web domains can access your object storage from client-side JavaScript. When a web application running on one domain attempts to access objects in HyperVault from a different domain, the browser checks CORS policies to determine if the request should be allowed. See the Mozilla CORS documentation for more information.

HyperVault supports two levels of CORS configuration:

  • Global CORS: Applies to all API endpoints and buckets using server-level settings
  • Bucket-specific CORS: Fine-grained control per bucket with up to 100 rules using mc cors commands

Bucket-level CORS configurations override the global settings.

Global CORS allowed origins

HYPERVAULT_API_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN
api cors_allow_origin

Optional

Specify a comma-separated list of origins allowed to access the HyperVault deployment. Defaults to * (all origins).

When set to *, HyperVault allows requests from any origin. For production deployments, specify explicit origins for better security.

Allow credentials with wildcard origins

HYPERVAULT_API_CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS_WITH_WILDCARD
api cors_allow_credentials_with_wildcard

Optional

Controls whether credentials are allowed when wildcard origin (*) is configured. Defaults to on for backwards compatibility.

When set to on and cors_allow_origin is *, HyperVault echoes back the requesting origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. While browsers accept this, it does not follow the CORS specification correctly.

When set to off, HyperVault does not return the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header for wildcard configurations, providing stricter CORS compliance.

For security hardening in production environments, set this to off to enforce proper CORS behavior according to the specification.

O_DIRECT writes

HYPERVAULT_API_ODIRECT
api odirect

Control O_DIRECT behavior for read and write operations. O_DIRECT bypasses the operating system page cache, reading from and writing directly to the disk.

Valid values:

  • on or read+write - Enable O_DIRECT for both reads and writes.
  • read - Enable O_DIRECT for reads only. Writes go through the page cache.
  • write - Enable O_DIRECT for writes only. Reads go through the page cache.
  • off - Disable O_DIRECT for both reads and writes.
Disabling O_DIRECT for writes can cause the page cache to grow unbounded, leading to memory pressure and potential out-of-memory conditions. It is never recommended to set this to off in production. Only disable for testing purposes with careful monitoring of system memory.

The default value is on.

Root access

HYPERVAULT_API_ROOT_ACCESS
api root_access

Enable or disable root credential access for all API calls, including S3 and admin operations. Set to off to prevent the root credentials from being used for S3 API operations, restricting them to admin operations only.

Valid values are on or off.

The default value is on.

Synchronous events

HYPERVAULT_API_SYNC_EVENTS
api sync_events

Enable synchronous bucket notifications. When enabled, HyperVault waits for notification delivery before completing the API response.

Valid values are on or off.

The default value is off.

Thread pressure check

HYPERVAULT_API_THREAD_PRESSURE_CHECK
api thread_pressure_check

Enable or disable thread pressure monitoring for health endpoints. When enabled, HyperVault tracks goroutine usage relative to system limits and can report health degradation through health check responses.

Valid values are on or off.

The default value is on.

Thread pressure warning threshold

HYPERVAULT_API_THREAD_PRESSURE_WARNING
api thread_pressure_warning

Set the thread pressure warning threshold as a ratio between 0 and 1. When thread usage exceeds this ratio of the system limit, HyperVault logs a warning.

The default value is 0.50.

Thread pressure critical threshold

HYPERVAULT_API_THREAD_PRESSURE_CRITICAL
api thread_pressure_critical

Set the thread pressure critical threshold as a ratio between 0 and 1. When thread usage exceeds this ratio, health endpoints return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests).

The default value is 0.85.

Maximum concurrent API requests

HYPERVAULT_API_REQUESTS_MAX
api requests_max

Optional

Set the maximum number of concurrent S3 and admin API requests allowed across all nodes of the cluster. The configured value is divided across the total node count to size each node’s per-node request pool.

The default value is auto, where HyperVault automatically calculates the limit based on available host RAM. See Memory Requirements for the formula used to derive the per-node limit.

Set an explicit integer to override the auto-derived limit. Reducing the concurrent request limit is a common tuning step for deployments using spinning (HDD) drives with high-concurrency workloads, where converting random I/O into sequential I/O improves drive efficiency.

mc admin config set ALIAS api requests_max=1600
mc admin service restart ALIAS

Or set the equivalent environment variable:

export HYPERVAULT_API_REQUESTS_MAX=1600
This is a server-wide concurrency cap distinct from the finer-grained per-bucket and per-access-key limits configured through mc qos rules.

List quorum

HYPERVAULT_API_LIST_QUORUM
api list_quorum

Optional

Set the minimum acceptable quorum for list operations.

Valid values are optimal, reduced, disk, strict, and auto.

The default value is strict.

Stale multipart upload expiry

HYPERVAULT_API_STALE_UPLOADS_EXPIRY
api stale_uploads_expiry

Optional

Set the duration after which an in-progress multipart upload with no activity is considered stale and eligible for automatic cleanup. Accepts a Go duration string such as 24h.

The default value is 24h.

This automatic, server-wide background cleanup is distinct from the per-bucket AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle action.

Stale multipart upload cleanup interval

HYPERVAULT_API_STALE_UPLOADS_CLEANUP_INTERVAL
api stale_uploads_cleanup_interval

Optional

Set how often HyperVault scans for and removes stale multipart uploads. Accepts a Go duration string such as 6h.

The default value is 6h.

Cluster readiness deadline

HYPERVAULT_API_CLUSTER_DEADLINE
api cluster_deadline

Optional

Set the deadline for the cluster readiness check. Accepts a Go duration string such as 10s.

The default value is 10s.

Remote transport deadline

HYPERVAULT_API_REMOTE_TRANSPORT_DEADLINE
api remote_transport_deadline

Optional

Set the deadline for API requests on remote transports while proxying between federated instances. Accepts a Go duration string such as 2h.

The default value is 2h.

Trash cleanup interval

HYPERVAULT_API_DELETE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL
api delete_cleanup_interval

Optional

Set how often HyperVault permanently deletes objects from the .trash folder. Accepts a Go duration string such as 5m.

The default value is 5m.

Trusted upstream proxies

HYPERVAULT_API_TRUSTED_UPSTREAM_PROXIES
api trusted_upstream_proxies

Optional

Specify a comma-separated list of upstream proxy IPs or CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, and RFC 7239 Forwarded headers are honored when deriving the client source IP. The derived source IP is used to evaluate aws:SourceIp IAM and bucket-policy conditions.

Accepted values:

  • An empty value (the legacy default) trusts all proxies. This preserves backward compatibility but allows any authenticated caller to spoof their source IP by injecting a forged forwarded header.
  • - trusts no proxies. Forwarded headers are ignored entirely and the immediate TCP peer is always used as the source IP. Use this when no reverse proxy sits in front of HyperVault.
  • A comma-separated list of IPs or CIDRs trusts only those peers. The X-Forwarded-For chain is walked right-to-left, and the first hop outside the trusted set becomes the source IP. Requests from untrusted peers are not rejected; they simply cannot dictate the source IP.
The empty default trusts all proxies. For deployments that rely on aws:SourceIp policy conditions, specify the trusted proxy IPs or CIDRs explicitly, or set this to - when no reverse proxy is present, to prevent source-IP spoofing.

Remote NTP server

HYPERVAULT_NTP_SERVER
This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Optional

Set a remote NTP server endpoint used as the time source instead of the system clock when computing object-lock and retention dates.

By default, HyperVault uses the server’s system time to compute retention dates.

Parquet S3 Select

HYPERVAULT_API_SELECT_PARQUET
This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Optional

Enable S3 Select support for Parquet-formatted objects.

The default value is off as a security mitigation, since hostile crafted Parquet input can crash the server. While disabled, the server rejects Parquet queries with the error parquet format parsing not enabled on server.

Set to on to enable Parquet S3 Select queries. Only enable this in controlled environments where it is safe to assume no hostile content can be uploaded to the cluster.

Extended object naming

Optional

HYPERVAULT_OBJECT_NAMING

Specifies the mode to use when writing objects to disk. Set to extended to have HyperVault convert special characters to allow writing on a filesystem.

Defaults to safe, which does not allow special characters in object or prefix names.

Requires HyperVault RELEASE.2025-12-20T04-58-37Z or later. Must be enabled at first run of HyperVault.

For more details on this mode, see Extended Backend.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.
text: Core Settings This page covers settings that control core behavior of the MinIO AIStor process. You can establish or modify settings by defining: an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the AIStor Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable. a configuration setting using mc admin config set. If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, MinIO AIStor uses the environment variable value. Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both. Each configuration setting controls fundamental MinIO AIStor behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production. Server CLI options Environment Variable MINIO_OPTS Optional Set a string of parameters to use when starting the AIStor Server. This environment variable only applies for systems using the default systemd service installed using first-party DEB or RPM packages. See Install MinIO AIStor on Linux for more information. Use the /etc/default/minio file and create an environment variable MINIO_OPTS for specifying parameters to append to the minio process started with systemctl service start minio: # Editing /etc/default/minio MINIO_OPTS=' --console-address=":9001" --ftp="address=:8021" --ftp="passive-port-range=30000-40000" ' If running minio on the command line or using a custom systemd unit file that omits MINIO_OPTS, use MINIO_ARGS instead: export MINIO_ARGS=' --console-address=":9001" --ftp="address=:8021" --ftp="passive-port-range=30000-40000" ' minio server ... # The above is equivalent to running the following: # minio server --console-address=":9001" \ # --ftp="address=:8021" \ # --ftp="passive-port-range=30000-40000" Configuration Setting There is no configuration setting for this variable, as these settings apply at server startup. MinIO AIStor license Environment Variable MINIO_LICENSE Path to the minio.license file downloaded from SUBNET. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option. Storage volumes Environment Variable MINIO_VOLUMES The directories or drives the minio server process uses as the storage backend. Functionally equivalent to setting minio server DIRECTORIES. Use this value when configuring MinIO AIStor to run using an environment file. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option. Address Environment Variable MINIO_ADDRESS Specifies the hostname and port on which the server listens for incoming connections. Equivalent to the following: CLI parameter minio server --address Configuration file setting address The order of precedence is as follows: Configuration file setting Environment variable CLI parameter Use this value when configuring MinIO AIStor to run using an environment file. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option. Console Address Environment Variable MINIO_CONSOLE_ADDRESS Specifies the hostname and port on which the web console listens for incoming connections. Equivalent to the following: CLI parameter minio server --console-address Configuration file setting console-address The order of precedence is as follows: Configuration file setting Environment variable CLI parameter Use this value when configuring MinIO AIStor to run using an environment file. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option. Environment variable file path Environment Variable MINIO_CONFIG_ENV_FILE Specifies the full path to the file the Object Store process uses for loading environment variables. For systemd-managed files, set this value to the path of the environment file (/etc/default/minio) to direct MinIO AIStor to reload changes to that file when using mc admin service restart to restart the deployment. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option. Workers for expiration Environment Variable MINIO_ILM_EXPIRY_WORKERS Specifies the number of workers to make available to expire objects configured with ILM rules for expiration. When not set, MinIO AIStor defaults to using up to half of the available processing cores available. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option. Domain Environment Variable MINIO_DOMAIN Enables Virtual Host-style requests to the MinIO AIStor deployment. Set the value to the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) for MinIO AIStor to accept incoming virtual host requests. Omitting this setting directs MinIO AIStor to only accept the default path-style requests. For example, consider a MinIO AIStor deployment with an assigned FQDN of minio.example.net. With path-style lookups, applications can access the bucket using its full path as minio.example.net/mybucket. With virtual-host lookups, application can access the bucket as a virtual host as mybucket.minio.example.net/. To configure more than one domain, set MINIO_DOMAIN to a comma-separated list of FQDNs, such as minio.example.net,s3.example.net. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option. Configure virtual-host-style requests Setting MINIO_DOMAIN alone is not sufficient. Because each bucket is addressed as a subdomain of the configured domain (mybucket.minio.example.net), the surrounding DNS and TLS configuration must also resolve and secure those subdomains. To support virtual-host-style addressing for a domain such as minio.example.net: Set MINIO_DOMAIN on every MinIO AIStor node. Set the environment variable to the domain (or comma-separated list of domains) on each server in the deployment and restart the nodes so the setting takes effect. export MINIO_DOMAIN=minio.example.net Create a wildcard DNS record. Add a wildcard DNS entry that resolves *.minio.example.net to the deployment (or to the load balancer in front of it), in addition to the existing record for the bare minio.example.net domain. Without the wildcard record, requests to mybucket.minio.example.net cannot reach the deployment. Use a TLS certificate that covers the wildcard domain. Virtual-host-style requests are sent to bucket subdomains, so the TLS certificate presented by MinIO AIStor (or by the load balancer terminating TLS) must include both the bare domain and the wildcard domain in its Subject Alternative Name (SAN) list: minio.example.net *.minio.example.net A certificate issued only for minio.example.net causes TLS hostname-verification errors when clients connect to mybucket.minio.example.net. Wildcard certificates match only a single label, so a nested path such as mybucket.sub.minio.example.net is not covered. Configure any load balancer or proxy to forward the wildcard host. If a load balancer or reverse proxy sits in front of the deployment, configure it to route *.minio.example.net to the MinIO AIStor nodes and to preserve the original Host header so MinIO AIStor can resolve the bucket from the request. After completing these steps, applications can address buckets either by path (minio.example.net/mybucket) or as a virtual host (mybucket.minio.example.net). Scanner speed Environment Variable MINIO_SCANNER_SPEED Configuration Setting scanner speed Manage the maximum wait period for the scanner when balancing MinIO AIStor read/write performance to scanner processes. MinIO AIStor utilizes the scanner for bucket replication, site replication, lifecycle management, and healing tasks. Valid values include: Setting Description fastest Removes scanner wait on read/write latency, allowing the scanner to operate at full-speed and IOPS consumption.This setting may result in reduced read and write performance. fast Sets a short scanner wait time on read/write latency, allowing the scanner to operate at a higher speed and IOPS consumption.This setting may result in reduced read and write performance. default Sets a moderate scanner wait time on read/write latency, allowing the scanner to operate at a balanced speed and IOPS consumption.This setting seeks to maintain read and write performance while allowing ongoing scanner activity. slow Sets a medium scanner wait time on read/write latency, where the scanner operates at a reduced speed and IOPS consumption.This setting allows better read and write performance while reducing scanner performance.May impact scanner-dependent features, such as lifecycle management and replication. slowest Sets a large scanner wait time on read/write latency, where the scanner operates at a substantially lower speed and IOPS consumption.This setting prioritizes read and write operations at the potential cost of scanner operations.May impact scanner-dependent features, such as lifecycle management and replication. Set to extended to have MinIO AIStor convert special characters to allow writing on a filesystem. Defaults to safe, which does not allow special characters in object or prefix names. Requires MinIO AIStor RELEASE.2025-12-20T04-58-37Z or later. Must be enabled at first run of MinIO AIStor. For more details on this mode, see Extended Backend. Configuration Setting This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

title: Deprecated Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Deprecated Settings

This page covers deprecated settings that control core behavior of the HyperVault Server process.

Settings on this page may be removed at any time. Users should migrate to the recommended replacement at the earliest opportunity.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault Server uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Environment variables

Any information listed in this section is here for historical reference only. All listed variables may be removed from a future release at any time.

HYPERVAULT_SERVER_URL

Deprecated since version RELEASE.2024-05-10T01-41-38Z

The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) the web console uses for connecting to the HyperVault Server.

For the Console to function correctly, the server URL must be the FQDN of the host, resolveable, and reachable.

If the specified value does not resolve to the server, logins using the console may fail and return a network error after a wait period. Older versions of the Console may return a generic ‘Invalid Login’ error instead. Unset the value or address the FQDN resolution issue to allow Console logins to proceed. This setting may be required if:

  • The server uses a TLS certificate that does not include the host local IP(s) in the certificate Subject Alternative Name (SAN).

or

  • The Console must use a specific hostname to connect or reference the server, such as due to a reverse proxy or similar configuration.

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_AZURE_USE_GROUP_ID

Deprecated since version RELEASE.2025-12-20T04-58-37Z

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_AZURE_USE_GROUP_ID
identity_openid azure_use_group_id

Replaced by HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_AZURE_TENANT_ID.

This setting enabled Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) group ID fetching using the Microsoft Graph API. The new azure_tenant_id setting provides the same functionality with improved configuration by allowing human readable configuration names explicitly linked to the Azure tenant’s UUID.

See Migrating from azure_use_group_id for migration instructions.

title: Etcd Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Etcd Settings

This page covers settings for connecting HyperVault to an external etcd cluster. Etcd provides a distributed key-value store used for DNS-based bucket routing with virtual-host-style access.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Endpoints

HYPERVAULT_ETCD_ENDPOINTS
etcd endpoints

Required

Specify a comma-separated list of etcd server endpoints. Setting this value enables the etcd integration.

All endpoints must use the same scheme (all http:// or all https://). When using https:// endpoints, HyperVault connects using TLS 1.2 or later.

export HYPERVAULT_ETCD_ENDPOINTS="https://etcd1.example.net:2379,https://etcd2.example.net:2379,https://etcd3.example.net:2379"

No default value. This setting must be explicitly configured to enable etcd.

Path prefix

HYPERVAULT_ETCD_PATH_PREFIX
etcd path_prefix

Optional

Set a namespace prefix for all keys stored in etcd. Use this to isolate multiple HyperVault deployments sharing the same etcd cluster.

No default value.

CoreDNS path

HYPERVAULT_ETCD_COREDNS_PATH
etcd coredns_path

Optional

Set the etcd path where HyperVault stores bucket DNS records for CoreDNS integration.

The default value is /skydns.

Client certificate

HYPERVAULT_ETCD_CLIENT_CERT
etcd client_cert

Optional

Path to the client certificate file for mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication with the etcd cluster. Must be specified together with client certificate key.

No default value.

Client certificate key

HYPERVAULT_ETCD_CLIENT_CERT_KEY
etcd client_cert_key

Optional

Path to the client private key file for mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication with the etcd cluster. Must be specified together with client certificate.

No default value.

title: Heal Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Heal Settings

This page covers settings that control data healing behavior for the HyperVault process. Healing automatically detects and repairs corrupted or missing data using erasure coding.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Bitrot scan

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_BITROTSCAN
heal bitrotscan

Enable bitrot scanning on local drives when the scanner checks objects. Bitrot scanning verifies data integrity by comparing stored checksums against computed values.

Valid values:

  • off - Disable bitrot scanning.
  • on - Enable continuous bitrot scanning every scanner cycle.
  • A duration such as 1m, 6m, or 1y - Enable bitrot scanning at the specified interval. Minimum interval is 1m (one month). Use d for days, m for months, y for years.

The default value is off.

Maximum sleep

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_MAX_SLEEP
heal max_sleep

Set the maximum sleep duration between objects to slow down heal operations. Use this to reduce the I/O impact of healing on production workloads.

Specify a Go-compatible duration string such as 50ms, 100ms, or 1s.

The default value is 50ms.

Maximum I/O

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_MAX_IO
heal max_io

Set the maximum number of I/O requests allowed between objects during healing. Together with maximum sleep, this controls healing throughput.

The default value is 50.

Dangling object handling

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_DANGLING
heal dangling

Controls how HyperVault handles dangling (stale) objects that no longer have valid erasure set references.

Valid values:

  • purge - Immediately remove dangling objects.
  • quarantine - Move dangling objects to a quarantine location. Objects remain quarantined for the duration specified by dangling expiry.
  • ignore - Take no action on dangling objects.

The default value is purge.

Transitioned (tiered) objects

Objects transitioned to a remote (warm) tier through lifecycle tiering are never treated as dangling and are never purged, regardless of how many xl.meta copies are lost on the primary (hot) tier drives.

For these objects, the data resides in the warm tier while only the xl.meta metadata is stored on the primary tier. Healing therefore restores only the xl.meta metadata. Before healing, HyperVault verifies that the warm-tier content is accessible by performing a small sample read. As long as at least one xl.meta copy and the tier configuration remain available, HyperVault rebuilds the metadata to all drives. If the warm tier is inaccessible, healing fails and requires manual intervention.

The hypervault_debug_heal_transitioned_object_total metric reports the number of transitioned objects processed by healing.

Dangling expiry

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_DANGLING_EXPIRY
heal dangling_expiry

Set the expiration duration for quarantined dangling objects. Only applies when dangling is set to quarantine.

Use d for days, m for months, y for years. The minimum value is 1d (one day).

The default value is 1y (one year).

Drive workers

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_DRIVE_WORKERS
heal drive_workers

Set the number of workers per drive used for fresh drive healing. Fresh drive healing populates replacement or newly added drives with data from existing erasure set members.

When set to 0, HyperVault automatically sets this to GOMAXPROCS/2.

The default value is 0 (automatic).

Auto healing

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_AUTO_HEALING
heal auto_healing

Enable or disable automatic healing of freshly connected or replaced drives. When enabled, HyperVault detects new or recovered drives and automatically initiates healing to restore data.

Valid values are on or off.

The default value is on.

Background workers

HYPERVAULT_HEAL_BACKGROUND_WORKERS
heal background_workers

Set the number of background heal workers per node. Background healing repairs objects identified by the scanner or the Most Recently Failed (MRF) queue.

When set to 0, HyperVault automatically sets this to GOMAXPROCS/2.

The default value is 0 (automatic).

title: Kubernetes Identity Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Kubernetes Identity Settings

This page documents settings for authenticating Kubernetes workloads with their own service account tokens. See Kubernetes Service Account Identity for how the provider works and how to grant policies with the PolicyBinding resource.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Enable

The identity_kubernetes subsystem has no enable setting.

HyperVault turns the provider on by itself when it detects that it runs inside a Kubernetes cluster and can reach both a token validator and the PolicyBinding API. To stop HyperVault from accepting service account tokens, set token_validation to disabled.

Settings

Token validation

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_KUBERNETES_TOKEN_VALIDATION
identity_kubernetes token_validation

How HyperVault validates a service account token. One of the following values:

Value Behavior
oidc Verify the token signature against the cluster’s OIDC discovery endpoint, caching signing keys. This is the default.
token_review Call the Kubernetes TokenReview API for every request.
disabled Do not accept service account tokens.

Default value: oidc

token_review places the Kubernetes API server in the path of every authentication. oidc calls out only when it meets a signing key it has not cached.

Token audience

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_KUBERNETES_TOKEN_AUDIENCE
identity_kubernetes token_audience

The audience HyperVault requires in a service account token. Project the token with a matching audience so the check succeeds.

Default value: sts.min.io

Keep the configured audience. An empty string turns the audience check off, which accepts any correctly signed service account token in the cluster, including tokens minted for other services.

title: LDAP Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
LDAP Settings

This page documents settings for enabling external identity management using an Active Directory or LDAP service. See Configure HyperVault for Authentication using Active Directory / LDAP for a tutorial on using these settings.

HyperVault supports configuring multiple LDAP providers. You provide a unique name for each provider configuration, allowing you to integrate with different directory services or organizational units within your environment.

HyperVault recommends using the mc idp ldap commands for LDAP management operations. These commands offer better validation and additional features, while providing the same settings as the identity_ldap configuration key.

The identity_ldap configuration settings remains available for existing scripts and other tools.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Examples

The following environment variables are required when defining an LDAP configuration.

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_SERVER_ADDR="ldapserver.com:636"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_DN="cn=hypervaultlookupuser,dc=example,dc=net"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_PASSWORD="userpassword"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_BASE_DN="dc=example,dc=net"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_FILTER="(&(objectCategory=user)(sAMAccountName=%s))"

The following settings are required when defining LDAP using mc admin config set:

mc admin config set identity_ldap                                       \
   enabled="true"                                                       \
   server_addr="ad-ldap.example.net/"                                   \
   lookup_bind_dn="cn=hypervaultlookupuser,dc=example,dc=net"                \
   lookup_bind_dn_password="userpassword"                               \
   user_dn_search_base_dn="dc=example,dc=net"                           \
   user_dn_search_filter="(&(objectCategory=user)(sAMAccountName=%s))"

Multiple LDAP configurations

Version Requirements
Support for multiple LDAP configurations requires HyperVault Server version RELEASE.2025-12-20T04-58-37Z or later and HyperVault Client (mc) version RELEASE.2025-12-19T20-11-44Z or later.

HyperVault supports multiple named LDAP configurations. The default configuration uses the name _ (underscore). Additional configurations use custom names that you specify when creating them.

Environment variable naming

To configure multiple LDAP providers using environment variables, append the configuration name to each variable name. The name is case-sensitive and must be consistent across all variables for the same configuration. By convention, use uppercase.

Default configuration (no suffix required, uses the ConfigName of _):

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_SERVER_ADDR="ldap1.example.com:636"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_DN="cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_PASSWORD="password"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_BASE_DN="dc=example,dc=com"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_FILTER="(&(objectCategory=user)(sAMAccountName=%s))"

Named configuration (append _CONFIGNAME suffix):

# Configuration named "partners"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_SERVER_ADDR_PARTNERS="ldap.partners.example.com:636"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_DN_PARTNERS="cn=admin,dc=partners,dc=com"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_PASSWORD_PARTNERS="password"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_BASE_DN_PARTNERS="dc=partners,dc=com"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_FILTER_PARTNERS="(&(objectCategory=user)(sAMAccountName=%s))"

CLI configuration

Use mc idp ldap add to create named LDAP configurations:

# Default configuration
mc idp ldap add ALIAS server_addr=ldap1.example.com:636 ...

# Named configuration "PARTNERS"
mc idp ldap add ALIAS PARTNERS server_addr=ldap.partners.example.com:636 ...

Use mc idp ldap ls to list all configured LDAP providers.

Settings

Server address

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_SERVER_ADDR
identity_ldap server_addr

Specify the hostname for the Active Directory / LDAP server. For example:

ldapserver.com:636

If your AD/LDAP server supports SRV Lookup Records, you can use the SRV Record Name configuration to identify the appropriate port for each hostname. If using that configuration, omit the port number from the provided server address.

Lookup bind DN

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_DN
identity_ldap lookup_bind_dn

Specify the Distinguished Name (DN) for an AD/LDAP account HyperVault uses when querying the AD/LDAP server. Enables Lookup-Bind authentication to the AD/LDAP server.

The DN account should be a read-only access keys with sufficient privileges to support querying performing user and group lookups.

Lookup bind password

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_LOOKUP_BIND_PASSWORD
identity_ldap lookup_bind_password

Specify the password for the Lookup-Bind user account.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

User DN search base DN

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_BASE_DN
identity_ldap user_dn_search_base_dn

Specify the base Distinguished Name (DN) HyperVault uses when querying for user credentials matching those provided by an authenticating client.

Separate multiple DNs with a semicolon (;).

For example:

cn=hypervaultusers,dc=myldapserver,dc=net;ou=swengg,dc=min,dc=io

Supports Lookup-Bind mode.

User DN search filter

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_SEARCH_FILTER
identity_ldap user_dn_search_filter

Specify the AD/LDAP search filter HyperVault uses when querying for user credentials matching those provided by an authenticating client.

Use the %s substitution character to insert the client-specified username into the search string. For example:

(userPrincipalName=%s)

User DN attributes

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_USER_DN_ATTRIBUTES
identity_ldap user_dn_attributes

Comma-separated list of user DN attributes.

Some valid values include, uid,cn,mail,sshPublicKey.

To enable public authentication for LDAP users, pass sshPublicKey as a DN attribute. The user can then use the passed SSH Public Key to log in to SFTP servers.

mc idp ldap update ALIAS user_dn_attributes=sshPublicKey

Enabled

Optional

This setting does not have an environment variable.

Use the configuration setting instead.

identity_ldap enable

Set to false to disable the AD/LDAP configuration.

If false, applications cannot generate STS credentials or otherwise authenticate to HyperVault using the configured provider.

Defaults to true or “enabled”.

Group search filter

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_GROUP_SEARCH_FILTER
identity_ldap group_search_filter

Specify an AD/LDAP search filter for performing group lookups for the authenticated user

Use the %s substitution character to insert the client-specified username into the search string. Use the %d substitution character to insert the Distinguished Name of the client-specified username into the search string.

For example:

(&(objectclass=groupOfNames)(memberUid=%s))

When configuring AD/LDAP group lookups, configure specific filters that return the minimum number of relevant groups for the purpose of supporting authentication.

Filters that return large group assignments increase the size of associated calls and resources. Functions sensitive to large request or response bodies may exhibit unexpected behaviors as a result.

Group search base DN

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_GROUP_SEARCH_BASE_DN
identity_ldap group_search_base_dn

Specify a semicolon-separated (;) list of group search base Distinguished Names HyperVault uses when performing group lookups.

For example:

cn=hypervaultgroups,dc=myldapserver,dc=net;ou=swengg,dc=min,dc=io

HyperVault carries a user’s group memberships inside the session token it issues, and the token bounds how large that list may be. A user in more groups than the bound admits cannot authenticate. At a typical distinguished name length the bound admits roughly a thousand groups, so reaching it means the search base or filter matches far more groups than the user needs. Narrow the group search so it returns only the groups you map to policies.

TLS skip verify

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
identity_ldap tls_skip_verify

Specify on to trust the AD/LDAP server TLS certificates without verification. This option may be required if the AD/LDAP server TLS certificates are signed by an untrusted Certificate Authority (for example, self-signed).

Defaults to off

Server insecure

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_SERVER_INSECURE
identity_ldap server_insecure

Specify on to allow unsecured (non-TLS encrypted) connections to the AD/LDAP server.

HyperVault sends AD/LDAP user credentials in plain text to the AD/LDAP server, such that enabling TLS is required to prevent reading credentials over the wire. Using this option presents a security risk where any user with access to network traffic can observe the unencrypted plaintext credentials.

Defaults to off.

Server start TLS

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_SERVER_STARTTLS
identity_ldap server_starttls

Specify on to enable StartTLS connections to an AD/LDAP server.

Defaults to off

For more about StartTLS, refer to section 4.14 of the LDAP RFC 4511 specification.

SRV record name

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_SRV_RECORD_NAME
identity_ldap srv_record_name

Specify the appropriate value to enable HyperVault to select an AD/LDAP server using a DNS SRV record request.

When enabled, HyperVault selects an AD/LDAP server by:

  • Constructing the target SRV record name following standard naming conventions.
  • Requesting a list of available AD/LDAP servers.
  • Choosing an appropriate target based on priority and weight.

The configuration examples below presume the AD/LDAP server address is set to example.com and the SRV record protocol is _tcp.

For SRV record names beginning with _ldap, specify ldap. The constructed DNS SRV record name resembles the following:

_ldap._tcp.example.com

For SRV record names with beginning with _ldaps, specify ldaps. The constructed DNS SRV record name resembles the following:

_ldaps._tcp.example.com

If your DNS SRV record name uses alternate service or protocol names, specify on and provide the full record name as your LDAP server address. Example: _ldapserver._specialtcp.example.com

For more about DNS SRV records, see DNS SRV Records for LDAP.

Comment

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_LDAP_COMMENT
identity_ldap identity_ldap comment

Specify a comment to associate to the AD/LDAP configuration.

title: Access Management Plugin Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Access Management Plugin Settings

This page documents settings for enabling external authorization management using the HyperVault Access Management Plugin. See HyperVault External Access Management Plugin for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. HyperVault strongly recommends testing configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Examples

When setting up the HyperVault Access Management plugin, you must define at minimum all required settings. The examples here represent the minimum required setting.

HYPERVAULT_POLICY_PLUGIN_URL="https://authzservice.example.net:8080/authz"

Use the mc admin config set command to create or update the access management plugin configuration. The policy_plugin url argument is required. Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" “)-delimited list.

mc admin config set policy_plugin                     \
   url="https://authzservice.example.net:8080/authz"  \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE] ...

Settings

URL

Required

HYPERVAULT_POLICY_PLUGIN_URL
policy_plugin url

The webhook endpoint for the external access management service (https://authzservice.example.net:8080/authz).

Auth token

Optional

HYPERVAULT_POLICY_PLUGIN_AUTH_TOKEN
policy_plugin auth_token

An authentication token to present to the configured webhook endpoint.

Specify a supported HTTP Authentication scheme as a string value, such as "Bearer TOKEN". HyperVault sends the token using the HTTP Authorization header.

HTTP2

Optional

HYPERVAULT_POLICY_PLUGIN_ENABLE_HTTP2
policy_plugin enable_http2

Enable experimental HTTP2 support for connecting to the configure webhook service.

Defaults to off

Comment

Optional

HYPERVAULT_POLICY_PLUGIN_COMMENT
policy_plugin comment

Specify a comment to associate to the external access management configuration.

title: Identity Management Plugin Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Identity Management Plugin Settings

This page documents settings for enabling external identity management using the HyperVault Identity Management Plugin. See HyperVault External Identity Management Plugin for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. HyperVault strongly recommends testing configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Examples

When setting up the HyperVault Identity Management Plugin, you must define at a minimum all of the required settings. The examples here represent the minimum required settings.

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_PLUGIN_URL="https://authservice.example.net:8080/auth"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_PLUGIN_ROLE_POLICY="ConsoleUser"

Use mc admin config set to create or update the identity plugin configuration. The identity_plugin url argument is required. Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" “)-delimited list.

mc admin config set identity_plugin                  \
   url="https://external-auth.example.net:8080/auth" \
   role_policy="consoleAdmin"                        \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE] ...

Settings

URL

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_PLUGIN_URL
identity_plugin url

The webhook endpoint for the external identity management service (https://authservice.example.net:8080/auth).

Role policy

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_PLUGIN_ROLE_POLICY
identity_plugin role_policy

Specify a comma-separated list of HyperVault policies to assign to authenticated users.

Enable

The identity_plugin subsystem has no enable setting.

HyperVault uses the plugin whenever url has a value, and ignores it when that value is empty. To stop using the plugin, clear the url setting.

While the plugin is unset, applications cannot generate STS credentials or otherwise authenticate to HyperVault through it.

Token

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_PLUGIN_AUTH_TOKEN
identity_plugin auth_token

An authentication token to present to the configured webhook endpoint.

Specify a supported HTTP Authentication scheme as a string value, such as "Bearer TOKEN". HyperVault sends the token using the HTTP Authorization header.

Role ID

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_PLUGIN_ROLE_ID
identity_plugin role_id

Specify a unique ID HyperVault uses to generate an ARN for this identity manager. HyperVault automatically adds an idmp- prefix to the specified ID when generating the ARN.

If omitted, HyperVault automatically generates the ID and prints the full ARN to the server log.

Comment

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_PLUGIN_COMMENT
identity_plugin comment

Specify a comment to associate to the identity configuration.

title: OpenID Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
OpenID Settings

This page documents settings for enabling external identity management using an OpenID Connect (OIDC)-compatible provider. See OpenID Connect Access Management for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. HyperVault strongly recommends testing configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Examples 

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CONFIG_URL="https://openid-provider.example.net/.well-known/openid-configuration"

Use mc admin config set to set or update the OpenID configuration. The config_url argument is required. Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" ")-delimited list.

mc admin config set identity_openid                                               \
  config_url="https://openid-provider.example.net/.well-known/openid-configuration" \
  [ARGUMENT="VALUE"] ...

Multiple configurations

HyperVault supports multiple named OpenID configurations. The default configuration uses the name _ (underscore). Additional configurations use custom names that you specify when creating them.

Environment variable naming

To configure multiple OpenID providers using environment variables, append the configuration name to each variable name. The name is case-sensitive and must be consistent across all variables for the same configuration. By convention, use uppercase.

Default configuration (no suffix required, uses the configuration name _):

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CONFIG_URL="https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLIENT_ID="hypervault-app"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLIENT_SECRET="secret"

Named configuration (append _CONFIGNAME suffix):

# Configuration named "PARTNERS"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CONFIG_URL_PARTNERS="https://partners-idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLIENT_ID_PARTNERS="hypervault-partners-app"
HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLIENT_SECRET_PARTNERS="partners-secret"

CLI configuration

Use mc idp openid add to create named OpenID configurations:

# Default configuration
mc idp openid add myhypervault \
   config_url="https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration" \
   client_id="hypervault-app" \
   client_secret="secret"

# Named configuration "PARTNERS"
mc idp openid add myhypervault PARTNERS \
   config_url="https://partners-idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration" \
   client_id="hypervault-partners-app" \
   client_secret="partners-secret"

Settings

Config URL

Required

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CONFIG_URL
identity_openid config_url

Specify the URL for the compatible provider discovery document.

The Discovery URL typically resembles the following:

https://openid-provider.example.net/.well-known/openid-configuration

Enabled

Optional

This setting does not have an environment variable.

Use the configuration setting instead.

identity_openid enable

Set to false to disable the OpenID configuration. Applications cannot generate STS credentials or otherwise authenticate to HyperVault using the configured provider if set to false. Defaults to true or “enabled”.

Client ID

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLIENT_ID
identity_openid client_id

Specify the unique public identifier HyperVault uses when authenticating user credentials against the compatible provider.

Client secret

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLIENT_SECRET
identity_openid client_secret

Specify the client secret HyperVault uses when authenticating user credentials against the compatible provider. This field may be optional depending on the provider.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

Role policy

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_ROLE_POLICY
identity_openid role_policy

Specify a comma-separated list of policy names to use for the request’s RoleArn for all authentication requests for the provider. The specified policy or policies must already exist on the HyperVault Server. To use this OIDC configuration, you must specify the corresponding RoleArn in the STS request body.

Claim name

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLAIM_NAME
identity_openid claim_name

Specify the name of the JWT Claim HyperVault uses to identify the policies to attach to the authenticated user. The claim can contain one or more comma-separated policy names to attach to the user. The claim must contain at least one policy for the user to have any permissions on the HyperVault server. Defaults to policy.

Claim prefix

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_CLAIM_PREFIX
identity_openid claim_prefix

Specify the JWT Claim namespace prefix to apply to the specified claim name.

Display name

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_DISPLAY_NAME
identity_openid display_name

Specify the user-facing name the Console UI displays on the login screen.

User ID claim

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_USER_ID_CLAIM
identity_openid user_id_claim

Specify the claim in the identity token whose value HyperVault reports as the user ID of an access key created through this provider.

Defaults to sub.

User-readable claim

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_USER_READABLE_CLAIM
identity_openid user_readable_claim

Specify the claim in the identity token whose value HyperVault reports as the human-readable display name of an access key created through this provider.

If unset, HyperVault reports no display name for these access keys.

Scopes

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_SCOPES
identity_openid scopes

Specify a comma-separated list of scopes. Defaults to those scopes advertised in the discovery document.

Dynamic URI redirect

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_REDIRECT_URI_DYNAMIC

Optional

Optional

Specify the OIDC Vendor to enable specific supported behaviors for that vendor.

Specify your Microsoft Entra ID tenant (directory ID). This setting is required when using Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) as the OIDC provider (vendor="azure").

To find your tenant ID:

  1. Go to the Azure Portal
  2. Navigate to Azure Active Directory > Overview
  3. Copy the Tenant ID (also called Directory ID)

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_KEYCLOAK_REALM
identity_openid keycloak_realm

Specify the Keycloak realm to use as part of Keycloak Admin API Operations, such as main.

Optional

identity_openid keycloak_admin_url

Specify the Keycloak Admin API URL. HyperVault can use this URL if configured to periodically validate authenticated Keycloak users as active/existing. For example, https://keycloak-endpoint:port/admin/.

Comment

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_OPENID_COMMENT

Specify a comment to associate with the compatible provider configuration.
