title: STS Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
STS Settings

This page documents settings for configuring Security Token Service (STS) behavior in HyperVault. STS provides temporary security credentials for users authenticated through external identity providers such as OpenID Connect or LDAP.

You can establish or modify these settings by defining environment variables on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.

These settings are environment variables only and do not have corresponding mc admin config settings.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. HyperVault strongly recommends testing configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Example 

export HYPERVAULT_STS_DURATION=1h
export HYPERVAULT_STS_SECURE=on
export HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_IP=10
export HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_LDAP_USER=5
export HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL=50

Settings

Duration

Optional

HYPERVAULT_STS_DURATION

The default lifetime for STS tokens issued by HyperVault. Specify as a Go duration string such as 1h, 30m, 24h, or 1h30m. This value applies when no explicit DurationSeconds parameter is provided in the STS request.

  • Valid Range: 15m (15 minutes) to 8760h (365 days)
  • Default: 1h (1 hour)

For example, to set the default STS token duration to 8 hours:

export HYPERVAULT_STS_DURATION=8h

To set the default STS token duration to 24 hours:

export HYPERVAULT_STS_DURATION=24h

Secure

Optional

HYPERVAULT_STS_SECURE

Require TLS for all STS operations. When enabled, STS endpoints only accept requests over HTTPS connections.

  • Valid Values: on, off
  • Default: off

HyperVault recommends enabling this setting in production environments to ensure STS operations occur over encrypted connections.

export HYPERVAULT_STS_SECURE=on

Token Revoke

Optional

HYPERVAULT_STS_TOKEN_REVOKE

Enable the STS token revocation feature. When enabled, administrators can revoke issued STS tokens before their expiration.

  • Valid Values: on, off
  • Default: off
export HYPERVAULT_STS_TOKEN_REVOKE=on

See Token revocation for usage instructions and mc commands.

Strict Expiration

Optional

HYPERVAULT_STS_STRICT_EXPIRATION

Control how HyperVault enforces STS token expiration.

  • Valid Values: on, off
  • Default: on

When enabled (default), HyperVault enforces strict token expiration based on the configured duration. When disabled, JWT token expiration claims may override the minimum or maximum allowed STS duration.

Keep this setting enabled unless your authentication workflow requires JWT claim-driven expiration.

export HYPERVAULT_STS_STRICT_EXPIRATION=on

Rate Limiting

HyperVault supports rate limiting STS endpoints to protect upstream identity providers from overload and prevent brute-force authentication attacks.

Rate Limit Per IP

Optional

HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_IP

The maximum number of STS requests per second allowed from a single source IP address on each node. This prevents a single source from flooding the STS endpoint, which could cascade to upstream identity provider lockout.

  • Valid Values: Non-negative integer (requests per second)
  • Default: 10
  • Special Value: 0 disables per-IP rate limiting
export HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_IP=10

Rate Limit Per LDAP User

Optional

HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_LDAP_USER

The maximum number of STS requests per second allowed for a specific LDAP user on each node. This prevents distributed attackers (many IPs) from locking out a specific LDAP user account by rate limiting based on the target username.

This setting applies only to LDAP-based STS authentication. LDAP is the only STS method where the username is sent as a plaintext parameter. Other methods (WebIdentity, ClientGrants, Certificate) use JWTs or certificates where brute-force is not a practical concern.

  • Valid Values: Non-negative integer (requests per second)
  • Default: 5
  • Special Value: 0 disables per-LDAP-user rate limiting
export HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_LDAP_USER=5

Rate Limit Global

Optional

HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL

The maximum number of total STS requests per second allowed on each node, across all IPs and users. This sets a ceiling on total STS authentication throughput per node, protecting upstream identity providers from overload.

  • Valid Values: Non-negative integer (requests per second)
  • Default: 50
  • Special Value: 0 disables global rate limiting
export HYPERVAULT_STS_RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL=50

Expiration Limits

HyperVault enforces the following limits on STS token expiration:

Limit Value
Minimum expiration 15m (15 minutes)
Maximum expiration 8760h (365 days)

These limits apply to both the HYPERVAULT_STS_DURATION setting and the DurationSeconds parameter in STS requests.

title: Certificate Identity Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Certificate Identity Settings

This page documents settings for authenticating clients with an X.509 client certificate. See AssumeRoleWithCertificate for the STS endpoint that uses them.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Settings

Enable

Required to use certificate identity

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_TLS_ENABLE

Set to on to accept AssumeRoleWithCertificate requests.

The certificate identity API is off until you set this environment variable. HyperVault reads the other settings on this page only when this variable is set, so setting them alone has no effect.

Skip verify

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
identity_tls skip_verify

Set to on to accept a client certificate without checking that a trusted certificate authority issued it.

Default value: off

Use this only when debugging
HyperVault takes the policy name from the certificate’s SPIFFE workload path, or from its subject common name. With this check off, any client can present a self-signed certificate naming any policy, including an administrative one, and receive credentials for it.

SPIFFE multi-domain

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_TLS_SPIFFE_MULTI_DOMAIN
identity_tls spiffe_multi_domain

Set to on to qualify the policy name from a SPIFFE identity with its trust domain, giving host/path rather than path.

Default value: off

Turn this on when you accept SVIDs from more than one trust domain, so that identical workload paths in different domains map to different policies.

URI SAN scheme

Optional

HYPERVAULT_IDENTITY_TLS_URI_SAN_SCHEME
identity_tls uri_san_scheme

Sets the URI SAN scheme that marks a client certificate as a workload identity.

Default value: spiffe

Set this when your certificate authority issues SPIFFE-shaped identities under another scheme, such as ans://example.org/billing/api. The scheme must start with a letter and may otherwise contain only letters, digits, +, -, and .. HyperVault lowercases the value and matches the certificate’s scheme without regard to case. HyperVault fails to start if the value does not match this syntax.

HyperVault recognizes only the scheme you set here. With uri_san_scheme set to ans, a certificate that presents a spiffe:// URI SAN is not a workload identity, and HyperVault maps it by subject common name instead.

The validation rules do not change. HyperVault substitutes the scheme and then applies the SPIFFE rules: the certificate must carry exactly one URI SAN, its trust domain must be lowercase, and its path must not be empty. A URI that carries user information, a port, a query, or a fragment is rejected.

Credential duration

Credentials from AssumeRoleWithCertificate use their own bounds rather than the STS settings:

Bound Value
Default 1 hour
Minimum 15 minutes
Maximum 365 days

HyperVault also shortens credentials that would outlive the certificate, so they expire no later than the certificate does.

title: ILM Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
ILM Settings

This page covers settings that control Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) for the HyperVault process.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Expiration workers

HYPERVAULT_ILM_EXPIRATION_WORKERS
ilm expiration_workers

Set the number of workers to use for expiring objects. Valid values are 1 to 500.

The default value is 100.

Transition workers

HYPERVAULT_ILM_TRANSITION_WORKERS
ilm transition_workers

Set the number of workers to use for transitioning objects to remote storage tiers. Valid values are 1 to 500.

The default value is 100.

  • Server Logs

  • Global Audit Event Queue

Prometheus authentication

HYPERVAULT_PROMETHEUS_AUTH_TYPE
This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Specifies the authentication mode for the Prometheus scraping endpoints.

Authentication Mode Description
jwt Default

Use mc admin prometheus generate to generate the necessary JWT bearer tokens.

html:
Audit Event Queue

The following section documents environment variables and configuration settings for customizing HyperVault’s global audit event queue. These settings control all configured audit targets.

Settings

Audit event queue dir

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_EVENT_QUEUE_DIR
audit_event_queue dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/audit/events.

HyperVault uses this directory for all configured webhook and audit targets.

Audit event queue dir max size

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_EVENT_QUEUE_DIR_MAX_SIZE
audit_event_queue dir_max_size

Specify the maximum size limit in megabytes (MB) of undelivered events to store in the specified queue dir. Defaults to 10000.

Audit event queue header filters

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_EVENT_QUEUE_HEADER_FILTERS
audit_event_queue header_filters

Specify a comma-separated list of HTTP headers to remove from audit log entries. When set, HyperVault removes the specified headers from both the request and response header fields in each audit log entry before sending it to configured audit targets.

Use this setting to filter sensitive or unnecessary headers from audit logs. For example, the following removes authorization and security token headers:

header_filters=Authorization,x-amz-security-token

Defaults to empty (no headers filtered).

Audit event queue flush timeout

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_EVENT_QUEUE_FLUSH_TIMEOUT
audit_event_queue flush_timeout

Specify the maximum time allowed for flushing events to disk on shutdown. Defaults to 30s.

title: Kafka Audit Logs | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Kafka Audit Logs

The following section documents environment variables for configuring HyperVault to publish audit logs to a Kafka broker.

The top-level configuration key for defining a Kafka broker target for publishing HyperVault audit logs.

Example 

export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS="https://kafka-endpoint.example.net:9092"

Use mc admin config set to set or update a Kafka audit target. Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" ")-delimited list.

mc admin config set audit_kafka \
   brokers="https://kafka-endpoint.example.net:9092" [ARGUMENTS=VALUE ...]

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_ENABLE
There is not a configuration setting for this value. Use the environment variable to disable a configured audit webhook target.

Set to “on” to enable the target. Set to “off” to disable the target.

Brokers

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_BROKERS
audit_kafka brokers

A comma-separated list of Kafka broker addresses.

Topic

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_TOPIC
audit_kafka topic

The name of the Kafka topic to associate to HyperVault audit log events.

TLS

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_TLS
audit_kafka tls

Set to “on” to enable TLS connectivity to the specified Kafka brokers. Defaults to “off”.

TLS skip verify

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
audit_kafka tls_skip_verify

Set to “on” to direct HyperVault to skip verification of the Kafka broker TLS certificates.

SASL

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL
audit_kafka sasl

Set to “on” to direct HyperVault to use SASL to authenticate against the Kafka brokers.

SASL username

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL_USERNAME
audit_kafka sasl_username

The SASL username HyperVault uses for authentication against the Kafka brokers.

SASL password

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL_PASSWORD
audit_kafka sasl_password

The SASL password HyperVault uses for authentication against the Kafka brokers.

SASL mechanism

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM
audit_kafka sasl_mechanism

The SASL mechanism HyperVault uses for authentication against the Kafka brokers. Defaults to plain.

SASL Kerberos realm

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_REALM
audit_kafka sasl_krb_realm

The realm name to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

SASL Kerberos keytab

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_KEYTAB
audit_kafka sasl_krb_keytab

The path to the HyperVault keytab to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

SASL Kerberos config path

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_CONFIG_PATH
audit_kafka sasl_krb_config_path

The path to the krb5.conf file to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

SASL Kerberos principal

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_PRINCIPAL
audit_kafka sasl_krb_principal

The principal name without realm suffix to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

TLS client auth

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH
audit_kafka tls_client_auth

An integer from 0 to 4 matching Go’s tls.ClientAuthType.

HyperVault presents its client certificate through client_tls_cert and client_tls_key. This setting maps to the ClientAuth field of the Go TLS configuration, which Go defines as the policy a TLS server applies to client authentication. Whether mutual TLS is required is determined by the Kafka broker.

HyperVault rejects the whole audit_kafka configuration if this value is not an integer.

Defaults to 0.

Client TLS cert

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_CLIENT_TLS_CERT
audit_kafka client_tls_cert

The path to the TLS client certificate to use for mTLS authentication.

Client TLS key

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_CLIENT_TLS_KEY
audit_kafka client_tls_key

The path to the TLS client private key to use for mTLS authentication.

Version

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_VERSION
audit_kafka version

The version of the Kafka broker HyperVault expects at the specified endpoints.

Max retry

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_MAX_RETRY
audit_kafka max_retry

The maximum number of times HyperVault retries sending a failed event before dropping it. A value of 0 retries indefinitely.

Defaults to 0.

Retry interval

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_RETRY_INTERVAL
audit_kafka retry_interval

The duration HyperVault waits between retries of a failed event, such as 10s. The maximum allowed value is 1m.

Defaults to 1s.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_COMMENT
audit_kafka comment

A comment to associate with the configuration.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_QUEUE_DIR
audit_kafka queue_dir
This option is deprecated. Use audit_event_queue instead.

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

Queue size

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_KAFKA_QUEUE_SIZE
audit_kafka queue_size
This option is deprecated. Use audit_event_queue instead.

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

title: Webhook Server Logs | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Webhook Server Logs

The following section documents settings for configuring HyperVault to publish hypervault server logs to an HTTP webhook endpoint. See Publish Server Logs to HTTP Webhook for more complete documentation and tutorials on using these settings.

Example

You can specify multiple webhook endpoints as log targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related logging environment variables. For example, the following settings define two distinct server log webhook endpoints:

export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_PRIMARY="TOKEN"
export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_PRIMARY="http://webhook-1.example.net"

export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_SECONDARY="TOKEN"
export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_SECONDARY="http://webhook-2.example.net"

You can specify multiple webhook endpoints as log targets by appending a unique identifier _ID to the configuration key. For example, the following settings define two distinct endpoints:

mc admin config set logger_webhook:primary \
   endpoint="http://webhook-01.example.net" [ARGUMENTS=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set logger_webhook:secondary \
   endpoint="http://webhook-02.example.net" [ARGUMENTS=VALUE ...]

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENABLE
logger_webhook

Specify “on” to enable publishing hypervault server logs to the HTTP webhook endpoint. Requires specifying HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT.

Webhook endpoint

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT
logger_webhook endpoint

The HTTP endpoint of the webhook.

Authentication token

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN
logger_webhook auth_token

An authentication token of the appropriate type for the endpoint. Omit for endpoints which do not require authentication. To allow for a variety of token types, HyperVault creates the request authentication header using the value exactly as specified. Depending on the endpoint, you may need to include additional information.

For example: for a Bearer token, prepend Bearer:

export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_myendpoint="Bearer 1a2b3c4f5e"

Modify the value according to the endpoint requirements. A custom authentication format could resemble the following:

export HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_xyz="ServiceXYZ 1a2b3c4f5e"

Consult the documentation for the desired service for more details.

Batch size

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_BATCH_SIZE
logger_webhook batch_size

Collect and send the specified number of events to the webhook as a batch. If not set, HyperVault sends one event per request.

Batch payload size

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_BATCH_PAYLOAD_SIZE
logger_webhook batch_payload_size

The maximum size in bytes of a batch payload sent to the webhook. The minimum is 32000.

Defaults to 1000000.

Client certificate

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_CERT
logger_webhook client_cert

The path to the mTLS certificate to use for authenticating to the webhook logger.

Client key

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_KEY
logger_webhook client_key

The path to the mTLS certificate key to use to authenticate with the webhook logger service.

Webhook proxy

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_PROXY
logger_webhook proxy

Define a proxy to use for the webhook logger when communicating from HyperVault to external webhooks.

TLS skip verification

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
logger_webhook tls_skip_verify

Specify true to direct HyperVault to skip verification of the remote webhook TLS certificates.

Defaults to false.

Max retry

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRY
logger_webhook max_retry

The maximum number of times HyperVault retries sending a failed event before dropping it. A value of 0 retries indefinitely.

Defaults to 0.

Retry interval

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_RETRY_INTERVAL
logger_webhook retry_interval

The duration HyperVault waits between retries of a failed event, such as 10s. The maximum allowed value is 1m.

Defaults to 1s.

HTTP timeout

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_HTTP_TIMEOUT
logger_webhook http_timeout

The maximum duration of each HTTP request, such as 10s. The minimum is 1s.

Defaults to 5s.

Encoding

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_ENCODING
logger_webhook encoding

Specify the encoding to use when sending events to the remote webhook. Supports either cbor or json encoding.

Defaults to json.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_DIR
logger_webhook queue_dir

Specify the directory path, such as /opt/hypervault/events, to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages. The HyperVault process must have read, write, and list access on the specified directory. HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the webhook service is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue size

HYPERVAULT_LOGGER_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_SIZE
logger_webhook queue_size

An integer value to use for the queue size for logger webhook targets.

title: Telemetry Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Telemetry Settings

This page covers settings that manage OpenTelemetry-formatted trace information for the HyperVault process. Trace capture supports ongoing troubleshooting and diagnostics.

The information can be relayed to a specified collector, recorded to a local encrypted or unencrypted file, or replayed from a local file to a collector.

You can also run the mc support telemetry commands for some of these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Enable

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_ENABLE
telemetry_target enable

Enable or disable telemetry collection on the specified target.

Valid values are on or off.

The default value is off.

Endpoint

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_ENDPOINT
telemetry_target endpoint

Required

IP address or FQDN and port of the OTLP-compatible collector that processes the data.

export HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_ENDPOINT="http://otlp.example.net:4318"

TLS

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_TLS
telemetry_target tls

Optional

Whether TLS is configured on the target endpoint.

Valid values are on or off.

The default value is off.

TLS skip verify

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
telemetry_target tls_skip_verify

Optional

Skip TLS certificate verification for the target endpoint.

Valid values are on or off.

The default value is off.

TLS client certificate

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_TLS_CLIENT_CERT
telemetry_target tls_client_cert

Optional

Path to the client certificate for mTLS authentication with the target server.

If not provided, HyperVault encrypts the telemetry file with the HyperVault public certificate.

TLS client key

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_TLS_CLIENT_KEY
telemetry_target tls_client_key

Optional

Path to the client private key for mTLS authentication with the target server.

If not specified, defaults to support_private.pem.

Sample rate

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_SAMPLE_RATE
telemetry_target sample_rate

A fraction, percentage, or float between 0 and 1 of the portion of calls to trace. Higher sample rates provide more complete data but have greater impact on system performance.

If not specified, defaults to 1.0 (all calls traced).

Trace type

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_TYPE
telemetry_target type

Optional

Include data for only the specified type(s) of traces, comma-separated. If not specified, defaults to s3.

Capitalization is ignored when specifying trace types.

Type Description
Admin Admin calls
BatchExpire Batch expiration operation calls
BatchKeyRotation Batch key rotation operation calls
BatchReplication Batch replication operation calls
Bootstrap Events during HyperVault cluster bootstrap
Decommission Decommission operation calls
Formatting Formatting events
FTP FTP server calls
Healing Healing operation calls
IAM Identity and access management calls
ILM Lifecycle management calls
Internal Calls to the .hypervault.sys/ folder
KMS Calls that interact with the configured KMS
Object Calls to the object layer
OS Golang OS package calls
Replication Replication events as they are picked up by workers
ReplicationResync Resync operation calls
Rebalance Rebalance operation calls
S3 S3 API calls
Scanner Scan operation calls
Storage Calls to the storage layer

Function name filter

HYPERVAULT_TELEMETRY_TARGET_FUNCNAME
telemetry_target funcname

Optional

Return traces only for calls that match the specified function name substring. Use this to narrow trace output to specific code paths.

title: Webhook Audit Logs | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Webhook Audit Logs

The following section documents environment variables for configuring HyperVault to publish audit logs to an HTTP webhook endpoint. See Publish Audit Logs to HTTP Webhook for more complete documentation and tutorials on using these environment variables.

Example

You can specify multiple webhook endpoints as audit log targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related logging settings.

For example, the following commands set two distinct audit log webhook endpoints:

export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_PRIMARY="TOKEN"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_PRIMARY="http://webhook-1.example.net"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_CERT_SECONDARY="/tmp/cert.pem"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_KEY_SECONDARY="/tmp/key.pem"

export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_SECONDARY="TOKEN"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_SECONDARY="http://webhook-1.example.net"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_CERT_SECONDARY="/tmp/cert.pem"
export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_KEY_SECONDARY="/tmp/key.pem"

Use mc admin config set to set or update an HTTP webhook target. Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" ")-delimited list.

You can specify multiple webhook endpoints as log targets by appending a unique identifier _ID to the configuration key. For example, the following settings define two distinct endpoints:

mc admin config set audit_webhook \
   endpoint="http://webhook.example.net" [ARGUMENTS=VALUE ...]

You can specify multiple HTTP webhook targets by appending [:name] to the top-level key. For example, the following commands set two distinct HTTP webhook targets as primary and secondary respectively:

mc admin config set audit_webhook:primary \
   endpoint="http://webhook-01.example.net" [ARGUMENTS=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set audit_webhook:secondary \
   endpoint="http://webhook-02.example.net" [ARGUMENTS=VALUE ...]

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENABLE

Specify “on” to enable publishing audit logs to the HTTP webhook endpoint. Requires specifying HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT.

Configure an audit webhook to enable it. There is not a separate enable configuration setting.

Webhook endpoint

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT
audit_webhook endpoint

The HTTP endpoint of the webhook.

Auth token

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN
audit_webhook auth_token

An authentication token of the appropriate type for the endpoint. Omit for endpoints which do not require authentication. To allow for a variety of token types, HyperVault creates the request authentication header using the value exactly as specified. Depending on the endpoint, you may need to include additional information.

For example, for a Bearer token, prepend Bearer:

export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_myendpoint="Bearer 1a2b3c4f5e"

Modify the value according to the endpoint requirements. A custom authentication format could resemble the following:

export HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_xyz="ServiceXYZ 1a2b3c4f5e"

Consult the documentation for the desired service for more details.

Batch size

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_BATCH_SIZE
audit_webhook batch_size

Collect and send the specified number of events to the webhook as a batch. If not set, HyperVault sends one event per request.

Batch payload size

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_BATCH_PAYLOAD_SIZE
audit_webhook batch_payload_size

The maximum size in bytes of a batch payload sent to the webhook. The minimum is 32000.

Defaults to 1000000.

Client certificate

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_CERT
audit_webhook client_cert

The x.509 client certificate to present to the HTTP webhook. Omit for webhooks which do not require clients to present a known TLS certificate.

Client key

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_KEY
audit_webhook client_key

The x.509 private key to present to the HTTP webhook. Omit for webhooks which do not require clients to present a known TLS certificate.

Webhook proxy

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_PROXY
audit_webhook proxy

Define a proxy to use for the webhook logger when communicating from HyperVault to external webhooks.

Max retry

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRY
audit_webhook max_retry

The maximum number of times HyperVault retries sending a failed event before dropping it. A value of 0 retries indefinitely.

Defaults to 0.

Retry interval

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_RETRY_INTERVAL
audit_webhook retry_interval

The duration HyperVault waits between retries of a failed event, such as 10s. The maximum allowed value is 1m.

Defaults to 1s.

TLS skip verification

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
audit_webhook tls_skip_verify

Specify true to direct HyperVault to skip verification of the remote webhook TLS certificates. Defaults to false.

HTTP timeout

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_HTTP_TIMEOUT
audit_webhook http_timeout

The maximum duration of each HTTP request, such as 10s. The minimum is 1s.

Defaults to 5s.

Encoding

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_ENCODING
audit_webhook encoding

Specify the encoding to use when sending events to the remote webhook. Supports either cbor or json encoding.

Defaults to json.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_DIR
audit_webhook queue_dir

Specify the directory path, such as /opt/hypervault/events, to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages. The HyperVault process must have read, write, and list access on the specified directory. HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the webhook service is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue size

HYPERVAULT_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_SIZE
audit_webhook queue_size

An integer value to use for the queue size for audit webhook targets. The default is 100000 events.

title: Notifications Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Notifications Settings

This page covers settings that control behavior related to HyperVault bucket notifications.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Sync events

Optional

HYPERVAULT_API_SYNC_EVENTS
api sync_events

Enables synchronous bucket notifications.

Specify on to direct HyperVault to wait until the remote target returns success on receipt of an event before processing further events.

Defaults to off, or asynchronous bucket notifications where HyperVault does not wait for the remote target to return success on receipt of an event.

Replication event threshold

HYPERVAULT_REPLICATION_EVENT_THRESHOLD

Optional

Specifies the time threshold for S3 Replication Time Control (RTC) events.

When an object takes longer than this threshold to replicate, HyperVault generates an s3:ObjectReplicationMissedThreshold event. When the object subsequently completes replication, HyperVault generates an s3:ObjectReplicationReplicatedAfterThreshold event.

These events allow monitoring of replication SLA compliance and identifying objects that exceed expected replication times.

Defaults to 15m (15 minutes). Minimum value is 1m (1 minute).

Value should be a duration string (for example, 5m, 30m, 1h).

Requires HyperVault RELEASE.2026-02-02T23-40-11Z or later.

This setting does not have a configuration setting option.

Notification targets

  • AMQP
  • Elasticsearch
  • Kafka
  • MQTT
  • MySQL
  • NATS
  • NSQ
  • PostgreSQL
  • Redis
  • Webhook

title: AMQP Notification Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
AMQP Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring an AMQP service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to AMQP (RabbitMQ) for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

You can specify multiple AMQP service endpoints by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related AMQP settings to the top level key.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_URL_PRIMARY="amqp://user:password@amqp-endpoint.example.net:5672"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_URL_SECONDARY="amqp://user:password@amqp-endpoint.example.net:5672"

You can specify multiple webhook endpoints as log targets by appending a unique identifier _ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_amqp:primary \
   url="user:password@amqp://amqp-endpoint.example.net:5672" [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set notify_amqp:secondary \
   url="user:password@amqp://amqp-endpoint.example.net:5672" [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Notice that for configuration settings, the unique identifier appends to amqp only, not to each individual argument.

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_ENABLE

Requires specifying HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_URL if set to on.

notify_amqp

Requires specifying notify_amqp url if set to on.

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to an AMQP endpoint.

Defaults to off.

URL

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_URL
notify_amqp url

Specify the AMQP server endpoint to which HyperVault publishes bucket events. For example, amqp://myuser:mypassword@localhost:5672.

Exchange

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_EXCHANGE
notify_amqp exchange

Specify the name of the AMQP exchange to use.

Exchange type

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_EXCHANGE_TYPE
notify_amqp exchange_type

Specify the type of the AMQP exchange.

Routing key

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_ROUTING_KEY
notify_amqp routing_key

Specify the routing key for publishing events.

Mandatory

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_MANDATORY
notify_amqp mandatory

Specify off to ignore undelivered messages errors. Defaults to on.

Durable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_DURABLE
notify_amqp durable

Specify on to persist the message queue across broker restarts. Defaults to off.

No wait

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_NO_WAIT
notify_amqp no_wait

Specify on to enable non-blocking message delivery. Defaults to off.

Internal

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_INTERNAL
notify_amqp internal

Specify on to use the exchange only if it is bound to other exchanges. See the RabbitMQ documentation on Exchange to Exchange Bindings for more information on AMQP exchange binding.

Auto deleted

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_AUTO_DELETED
notify_amqp auto_deleted

Specify on to automatically delete the message queue if there are no consumers. Defaults to off.

Delivery mode

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_DELIVERY_MODE
notify_amqp delivery_mode

Specify 1 for set the delivery mode to non-persistent queue.

Specify 2 to set the delivery mode to persistent queue.

Publisher confirms

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_PUBLISHING_CONFIRMS
notify_amqp publisher_confirms

Specify on to enable consumer acknowledgements and publisher confirms. Use this together with queue_dir for guaranteed delivery of all events.

Defaults to off.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_QUEUE_DIR
notify_amqp queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the AMQP service is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_amqp queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_AMQP_COMMENT
notify_amqp comment

Specify a comment for the AMQP configuration.

html:
Elasticsearch Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring an Elasticsearch service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to Elasticsearch for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Example

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_URL_PRIMARY="https://user:password@elasticsearch-endpoint.example.net:9200"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_URL_SECONDARY="https://user:password@elasticsearch-endpoint.example.net:9200"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEX_SECONDARY="bucketevents"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_FORMAT_SECONDARY="namespace"

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_elasticsearch:primary \
   url="user:password@https://elasticsearch-endpoint.example.net:9200" \
   index="bucketevents" \
   format="namespace" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set notify_elasticsearch:secondary \
   url="user:password@https://elasticsearch-endpoint.example.net:9200" \
   index="bucketevents" \
   format="namespace" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_ENABLE
notify_elasticsearch

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to an Elasticsearch service endpoint. Defaults to off.

URL

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_URL
notify_elasticsearch url

Specify the Elasticsearch service endpoint to which HyperVault publishes bucket events. For example, https://elasticsearch.example.com:9200. HyperVault supports passing authentication information using as URL parameters using the format PROTOCOL://USERNAME:PASSWORD@HOSTNAME:PORT.

HyperVault checks the health of the specified URL (if it is resolvable and reachable) prior to adding the target. HyperVault adds offline targets without blocking.

Index

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_INDEX
notify_elasticsearch index

Specify the name of the Elasticsearch index in which to store or update HyperVault bucket events. Elasticsearch automatically creates the index if it does not exist.

Format

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_FORMAT
notify_elasticsearch format

Specify the format of event data written to the Elasticsearch index. HyperVault supports the following values:

  • namespace: For each bucket event, HyperVault creates a JSON document with the bucket and object name from the event as the document ID and the actual event as part of the document body. Additional updates to that object modify the existing index entry for that object. Similarly, deleting the object also deletes the corresponding index entry.
  • access: For each bucket event, HyperVault creates a JSON document with the event details and appends it to the index with an Elasticsearch-generated random ID. Additional updates to an object result in new index entries, and existing entries remain unmodified.

Username

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_USERNAME
notify_elasticsearch username

The username for connecting to an Elasticsearch service endpoint which enforces authentication.

Password

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD
notify_elasticsearch password

The password for connecting to an Elasticsearch service endpoint which enforces authentication.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_QUEUE_DIR
notify_elasticsearch queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the Elasticsearch service is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_elasticsearch queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_ELASTICSEARCH_COMMENT
notify_elasticsearch comment

Specify a comment to associate with the Elasticsearch configuration.

title: Kafka Notification Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Kafka Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring an Kafka service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to Kafka for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Example

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_BROKERS_PRIMARY="https://kafka1.example.net:9200, https://kafka2.example.net:9200"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_BROKERS_SECONDARY="https://kafka1.example.net:9200, https://kafka2.example.net:9200"

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_kafka:primary \
   brokers="https://kafka1.example.net:9200, https://kafka2.example.net:9200"
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set notify_kafka:secondary \
   brokers="https://kafka1.example.net:9200, https://kafka2.example.net:9200"
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Notice that for configuration settings, the unique identifier appends to notify_kafka only, not to each individual argument.

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_ENABLE
notify_kafka

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to a Kafka endpoint. Defaults to off.

Brokers

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_BROKERS
notify_kafka brokers

Specify a comma-separated list of Kafka broker addresses. For example: "kafka1.example.com:2021,kafka2.example.com:2021"

HyperVault checks the health of the specified URL (if it is resolvable and reachable) prior to adding the target. HyperVault adds offline targets without blocking.

Topic

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_TOPIC
notify_kafka topic

Specify the Kafka topic to which HyperVault publishes events.

SASL

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL
notify_kafka sasl

Specify on to enable SASL authentication to the Kafka service endpoint. Defaults to off.

HyperVault ignores the other SASL settings, including the mechanism, the username, and the password, while this setting is off.

SASL username

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL_USERNAME
notify_kafka sasl_username

Specify the SASL username for authenticating to the Kafka service endpoint.

SASL password

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL_PASSWORD
notify_kafka sasl_password

Specify the SASL password for authenticating to the Kafka service endpoint.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

SASL Kerberos realm

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_REALM
notify_kafka sasl_krb_realm

The realm name to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

SASL Kerberos keytab

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_KEYTAB
notify_kafka sasl_krb_keytab

The path to the HyperVault keytab to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

SASL Kerberos config path

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_CONFIG_PATH
notify_kafka sasl_krb_config_path

The path to the krb5.conf file to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

SASL Kerberos principal

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL_KRB_PRINCIPAL
notify_kafka sasl_krb_principal

The principal name without realm suffix to use with SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_QUEUE_DIR
notify_kafka queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable a persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the Kafka server/broker is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_kafka queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_COMMENT
notify_kafka comment

Specify a comment to associate with the Kafka configuration.

SASL mechanism

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM
notify_kafka sasl_mechanism

Specify the SASL mechanism to use for authenticating to the Kafka broker(s). HyperVault supports the following mechanisms:

  • SHA512 for SCRAM-SHA-512
  • SHA256 for SCRAM-SHA-256
  • GSSAPI for Kerberos

Any other value, including an unset one, selects PLAIN.

TLS client auth

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH
notify_kafka tls_client_auth

Specify the client authentication type of the Kafka broker(s). The following table lists the supported values and their mappings:

Value Authentication Type
0 NoClientCert
1 RequestClientCert
2 RequireAnyClientCert
3 VerifyClientCertIfGiven
4 RequireAndVerifyClientCert

See ClientAuthType for more information on each client auth type.

Defaults to 0.

TLS

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_TLS
notify_kafka tls

Specify on to enable TLS connectivity to the Kafka broker(s).

TLS skip verify

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
notify_kafka tls_skip_verify

Enables or disables TLS verification of the Kafka broker(s) TLS certificates.

  • Specify on to disable TLS verification (Default).
  • Specify off to enable TLS verification.

Client TLS cert

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_CLIENT_TLS_CERT
notify_kafka client_tls_cert

Specify the path to the client certificate to use for performing mTLS authentication to the Kafka broker(s).

Client TLS key

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_CLIENT_TLS_KEY
notify_kafka client_tls_key

Specify the path to the client private key to use for performing mTLS authentication to the Kafka broker(s).

Version

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_VERSION
notify_kafka version

Specify the version of the Kafka cluster to assume when performing operations against that cluster. See the sarama reference documentation for more information on this field’s behavior.

Batch size

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_BATCH_SIZE
notify_kafka batch_size

Specify the integer value to use as the batch size for sending records to Kafka.

version changed
Changed in version RELEASE.2023-12-02T10-51-33Z: HyperVault previously limited this value to 100.

Batch commit timeout

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_BATCH_COMMIT_TIMEOUT
notify_kafka batch_commit_timeout

The commit timeout for the batch, such as 10s. HyperVault uses this setting only when batch_size is greater than 1.

Defaults to 0s.

Compression codec

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_PRODUCER_COMPRESSION_CODEC
notify_kafka compression_codec

Specify the compression codec to use when sending records to Kafka.

Supports the following values:

  • none
  • snappy
  • gzip
  • lz4
  • zstd
version added
New in version Object: Store RELEASE.2023-12-09T18-17-51Z

Compression level

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_KAFKA_PRODUCER_COMPRESSION_LEVEL
notify_kafka compression_level

Controls the level of compression applied based on the configured compression codec.

Specify an integer value greater than or equal to 0. The effect of the value depends on the selected codec.

version added
New in version Object: Store RELEASE.2023-12-09T18-17-51Z

title: MQTT Notification Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
MQTT Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring an MQTT service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to MQTT for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_BROKER_PRIMARY="tcp://user:password@mqtt-endpoint.example.net:1883"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_BROKER_SECONDARY="tcp://user:password@mqtt-endpoint.example.net:1883"

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_mqtt:primary \
   broker="tcp://endpoint:port" \
   topic="hypervault/bucket-name/events/" \
   username="username" \
   password="password" \
   [ARGUMENT="VALUE"] ... \

mc admin config set notify_mqtt:secondary \
   broker="tcp://endpoint:port" \
   topic="hypervault/bucket-name/events/" \
   username="username" \
   password="password" \
   [ARGUMENT="VALUE"] ...

With these settings, HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_ENABLE_PRIMARY indicates the environment variable is associated to an MQTT service endpoint with an ID of PRIMARY.

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_ENABLE
notify_mqtt

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to an MQTT endpoint. Defaults to off.

Broker

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_BROKER
notify_mqtt broker

Specify the MQTT server/broker endpoint. HyperVault supports TCP, TLS, or Websocket connections to the server/broker URL. For example:

  • tcp://mqtt.example.net:1883
  • tls://mqtt.example.net:1883
  • ws://mqtt.example.net:1883
version changed
Changed in version RELEASE.2023-05-27T05-56-19Z: HyperVault checks the health of the specified URL (if it is resolvable and reachable) prior to adding the target. HyperVault adds offline targets without blocking.

Topic

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_TOPIC
notify_mqtt topic

Specify the name of the MQTT topic to associate with events published by HyperVault to the MQTT endpoint.

Username

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_USERNAME
notify_mqtt username

Specify the MQTT username HyperVault should use to authenticate to the MQTT server/broker.

Password

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_PASSWORD
notify_mqtt password

Specify the password for the MQTT username HyperVault uses to authenticate to the MQTT server/broker.

version changed
Changed in version RELEASE.2023-06-23T20-26-00Z: HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

QoS

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_QOS
notify_mqtt qos

Specify the Quality of Service priority for the published events. Defaults to 0.

Keep alive interval

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_KEEP_ALIVE_INTERVAL
notify_mqtt keep_alive_interval

Specify the keep-alive interval for the MQTT connections. HyperVault supports the following units of time measurement:

  • s - seconds, “60s”
  • m - minutes, “60m”
  • h - hours, “24h”
  • d - days, “7d”

Reconnect interval

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_RECONNECT_INTERVAL
notify_mqtt reconnect_interval

Specify the reconnect interval for the MQTT connections. HyperVault supports the following units of time measurement:

  • s - seconds, “60s”
  • m - minutes, “60m”
  • h - hours, “24h”
  • d - days, “7d”

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MQTT_QUEUE_DIR
notify_mqtt queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the MQTT server/broker is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

title: MySQL Notification Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
MySQL Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring a MYSQL service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to MySQL for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_DSN_STRING_PRIMARY="username:password@tcp(mysql.example.com:3306)/hypervaultdb"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_TABLE_PRIMARY="hypervaultevents"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_FORMAT_PRIMARY="namespace"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_DSN_STRING_SECONDARY="username:password@tcp(mysql.example.com:3306)/hypervaultdb"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_TABLE_SECONDARY="hypervaultevents"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_FORMAT_SECONDARY="namespace"

With these settings, HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_ENABLE_PRIMARY indicates the environment variable is associated to a MySQL service endpoint with ID of PRIMARY.

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_mysql:primary \
   dsn_string="username:password@tcp(mysql.example.com:3306)/hypervaultdb"
   table="hypervaultevents" \
   format="namespace" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set notify_mysql:secondary \
   dsn_string="username:password@tcp(mysql.example.com:3306)/hypervaultdb"
   table="hypervaultevents" \
   format="namespace" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_ENABLE

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to a MySQL service endpoint.

Defaults to off.

Requires specifying the following additional environment variables if set to on:

  • HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_DSN_STRING
  • HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_TABLE
  • HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_FORMAT

notify_mysql

The top-level configuration key for defining an MySQL service endpoint for use with HyperVault bucket notifications.

Use mc admin config set to set or update an MySQL service endpoint. The following arguments are required for each target:

  • dsn_string
  • table
  • format

Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" ")-delimited list.

mc admin config set notify_mysql \
  dsn_string="username:password@tcp(mysql.example.com:3306)/hypervaultdb"
  table="hypervaultevents" \
  format="namespace" \
  [ARGUMENT="VALUE"] ...

DSN string

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_DSN_STRING
notify_mysql dsn_string

Specify the data source name (DSN) of the MySQL service endpoint. HyperVault expects the following format:

<user>:<password>@tcp(<host>:<port>)/<database>

For example:

"username:password@tcp(mysql.example.com:3306)/hypervaultdb"

version changed
Changed in version RELEASE.2023-05-27T05-56-19Z: HyperVault checks the health of the specified URL (if it is resolvable and reachable) prior to adding the target. HyperVault adds offline targets without blocking.

Table

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_TABLE
notify_mysql table

Specify the name of the MySQL table to which HyperVault publishes event notifications.

Format

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_FORMAT
notify_mysql format

Specify the format of event data written to the MySQL service endpoint. HyperVault supports the following values:

namespace
For each bucket event, HyperVault creates a JSON document with the bucket and object name from the event as the document ID and the actual event as part of the document body. Additional updates to that object modify the existing table entry for that object. Similarly, deleting the object also deletes the corresponding table entry.
access
For each bucket event, HyperVault creates a JSON document with the event details and appends it to the table with a MySQL-generated random ID. Additional updates to an object result in new index entries, and existing entries remain unmodified.

Max open connections

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_MAX_OPEN_CONNECTIONS
notify_mysql max_open_connections

Specify the maximum number of open connections to the MySQL database. Defaults to 2.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_QUEUE_DIR
notify_mysql queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the MySQL server/broker is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_mysql queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_MYSQL_COMMENT
notify_mysql comment

Specify a comment to associate with the MySQL configuration.

title: NATS Notification Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
NATS Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring an NATS service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to NATS for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Example

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_ADDRESS_PRIMARY="nats-endpoint.example.net:4222"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_ADDRESS_SECONDARY="nats-endpoint.example.net:4222"

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_nats:primary \
   address="nats-endpoint.example.com:4222" \
   subject="hypervaultevents" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set notify_nats:secondary \
   address="nats-endpoint.example.com:4222" \
   subject="hypervaultevents" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_ENABLE
notify_nats

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to an NATS service endpoint. Defaults to off.

Address

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_ADDRESS
notify_nats address

Specify the NATS service endpoint to which HyperVault publishes bucket events. For example, nats-endpoint.example.com:4222.

HyperVault checks the health of the specified URL (if it is resolvable and reachable) prior to adding the target. HyperVault adds offline targets without blocking.

Subject

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_SUBJECT
notify_nats subject

Specify the subscription to which HyperVault associates events published to the NATS endpoint.

Username

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_USERNAME
notify_nats username

Specify the username for connecting to the NATS service endpoint.

Password

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_PASSWORD
notify_nats password

Specify the password for connecting to the NATS service endpoint.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

Token

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_TOKEN
notify_nats token

Specify the token for connecting to the NATS service endpoint.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

User credentials

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_USER_CREDENTIALS
notify_nats user_credentials

Specify the path to the user credentials file https://docs.nats.io/using-nats/developer/connecting/creds to use to connect to the NATS service endpoint.

TLS

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_TLS
notify_nats tls

Specify on to enable TLS connectivity to the NATS service endpoint.

TLS skip verify

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
notify_nats tls_skip_verify

Enables or disables TLS verification of the NATS service endpoint TLS certificates.

  • Specify on to disable TLS verification (Default).
  • Specify off to enable TLS verification.

Ping interval

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_PING_INTERVAL
notify_nats ping_interval

Specify the duration interval for client pings to the NATS server. HyperVault supports the following time units:

  • s - seconds, "60s"
  • m - minutes, "5m"
  • h - hours, "1h"
  • d - days, "1d"

Jetstream

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_JETSTREAM
notify_nats jetstream

Specify on to enable JetStream support for streaming events to a NATS JetStream service endpoint.

Streaming

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_STREAMING
notify_nats streaming

Specify on to enable asynchronous publishing of events to the NATS service endpoint.

Streaming async

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_STREAMING_ASYNC
notify_nats streaming_async

Specify on to enable asynchronous publishing of events to the NATS service endpoint.

Streaming max pub acks in flight

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_STREAMING_MAX_PUB_ACKS_IN_FLIGHT
notify_nats streaming_max_pub_acks_in_flight

Specify the number of messages to publish without waiting for an ACK response from the NATS service endpoint.

Streaming cluster ID

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_STREAMING_CLUSTER_ID
notify_nats streaming_cluster_id

Specify the unique ID for the NATS streaming cluster.

Cert authority

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_CERT_AUTHORITY
notify_nats cert_authority

Specify the path to the Certificate Authority chain used to sign the NATS service endpoint TLS certificates.

Client cert

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_CLIENT_CERT
notify_nats client_cert

Specify the path to the client certificate to use for performing mTLS authentication to the NATS service endpoint.

Client key

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_CLIENT_KEY
notify_nats client_key

Specify the path to the client private key to use for performing mTLS authentication to the NATS service endpoint.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_QUEUE_DIR
notify_nats queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the NATS server/broker is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_nats queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NATS_COMMENT
notify_nats comment

Specify a comment to associate with the NATS configuration.

The top-level configuration key for defining an NSQ server/broker endpoint for use with HyperVault bucket notifications.

Use mc admin config set to set or update an NSQ server/broker endpoint. The following arguments are required for each endpoint:

  • nsqd_address
  • topic

Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" ")-delimited list.

mc admin config set notify_nsq                          \
   nsqd_address="https://nsq-endpoint.example.net:4150" \
   topic="<string>"                                     \
   [ARGUMENT="VALUE"] ...

NSQD address

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NSQ_NSQD_ADDRESS
notify_nsq nsqd_address

Specify the NSQ Daemon server address to which HyperVault publishes bucket events.

Topic

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NSQ_TOPIC
notify_nsq topic

Specify the topic to which HyperVault publishes events in the NSQ service.

TLS

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NSQ_TLS
notify_nsq tls

Specify on to enable TLS connectivity to the NSQ service broker.

TLS skip verify

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NSQ_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
notify_nsq tls_skip_verify

Enables or disables TLS verification of the NSQ service broker TLS certificates.

  • Specify on to disable TLS verification (Default).
  • Specify off to enable TLS verification.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NSQ_QUEUE_DIR
notify_nsq queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the NSQ server/broker is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NSQ_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_nsq queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_NSQ_COMMENT
notify_nsq comment

Specify a comment to associate with the NSQ configuration.

title: PostgreSQL Notification Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
PostgreSQL Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring an POSTGRES service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to PostgreSQL for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING_PRIMARY="host=postgresql-endpoint.example.net port=4222..."
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_TABLE_PRIMARY="hypervaultevents"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_FORMAT_PRIMARY="namespace"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING_SECONDARY="host=postgresql-endpoint.example.net port=4222..."
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_TABLE_SECONDARY="hypervaultevents"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_FORMAT_SECONDARY="namespace"

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_postgres:primary \
   connection_string="host=postgresql.example.com port=5432..."
   table="hypervaultevents" \
   format="namespace" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set notify_postgres:secondary \
   connection_string="host=postgresql.example.com port=5432..."
   table="hypervaultevents" \
   format="namespace" \
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

With these settings, HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_ENABLE_PRIMARY indicates the environment variable is associated to an PostgreSQL service endpoint with ID of PRIMARY.

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_ENABLE

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to a PostgreSQL service endpoint.

Defaults to off.

Requires specifying the following additional environment variables if set to on:

  • HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING
  • HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_TABLE
  • HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_FORMAT

notify_postgres

The top-level configuration key for defining an PostgreSQL service endpoint for use with HyperVault bucket notifications.

Use mc admin config set to set or update an PostgreSQL service endpoint. The following arguments are required for each target:

  • connection_string
  • table
  • format

Specify additional optional arguments as a whitespace (" ")-delimited list.

mc admin config set notify_postgres                            \
  connection_string="host=postgresql.example.com port=5432..." \
  table="hypervaultevents"                                          \
  format="namespace"                                           \
  [ARGUMENT="VALUE"] ...

Connection string

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING
notify_postgres connection_string

Specify the PostgreSQL connection string to which HyperVault publishes bucket events.

Table

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_TABLE
notify_postgres table

Specify the name of the PostgreSQL table to which HyperVault publishes event notifications.

Format

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_FORMAT
notify_postgres format

Specify the format of event data written to the PostgreSQL service endpoint.

Max open connections

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_MAX_OPEN_CONNECTIONS
notify_postgres max_open_connections

The maximum number of open connections to the PostgreSQL database.

Defaults to 2.

Queue dir

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_QUEUE_DIR
notify_postgres queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the PostgreSQL server/broker is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_postgres queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_POSTGRES_COMMENT
notify_postgres comment

Specify a comment to associate with the PostgreSQL configuration.

title: Webhook Notification Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Webhook Notification Settings

This page documents settings for configuring an Webhook service as a target for Bucket Notifications. See Publish Events to Webhook for a tutorial on using these settings.

You can establish or modify settings by defining:

  • an environment variable on the host system prior to starting or restarting the HyperVault Server. Refer to your operating system’s documentation for how to define an environment variable.
  • a configuration setting using mc admin config set.

If you define both an environment variable and the similar configuration setting, HyperVault uses the environment variable value.

Some settings have only an environment variable or a configuration setting, but not both.

Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Example

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_PRIMARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_PRIMARY="https://webhook1.example.net"

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_SECONDARY="on"
export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_SECONDARY="https://webhook1.example.net"

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set notify_webhook:primary \
   endpoint="https://webhook1.example.net"
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

mc admin config set notify_webhook:secondary \
   endpoint="https://webhook2.example.net"
   [ARGUMENT=VALUE ...]

Settings

Enable

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_ENABLE
notify_webhook

Specify on to enable publishing bucket notifications to a Webhook service endpoint. Defaults to off.

Endpoint

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT
notify_webhook endpoint

Specify the URL for the webhook service.

HyperVault checks the health of the specified URL (if it is resolvable and reachable) prior to adding the target. HyperVault adds offline targets without blocking.

Auth token

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN
notify_webhook auth_token

An authentication token of the appropriate type for the endpoint. Omit for endpoints which do not require authentication.

To allow for a variety of token types, HyperVault creates the request authentication header using the value exactly as specified. Depending on the endpoint, you may need to include additional information. For example, for a Bearer token, prepend Bearer:

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_myendpoint="Bearer 1a2b3c4f5e"

Modify the value according to the endpoint requirements. A custom authentication format could resemble the following:

export HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN_xyz="ServiceXYZ 1a2b3c4f5e"

Consult the documentation for the desired service for more details.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

Client cert

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_CERT
notify_webhook client_cert

Specify the path to the client certificate to use for performing mTLS authentication to the webhook service.

Client key

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_KEY
notify_webhook client_key

Specify the path to the client private key to use for performing mTLS authentication to the webhook service.

Comment

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_COMMENT
notify_webhook comment

Specify a comment to associate with the Webhook configuration.

Queue dir

This value is deprecated.

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_DIR
notify_webhook queue_dir

Specify the directory path to enable HyperVault’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/hypervault/events.

HyperVault stores undelivered events in the specified store while the webhook service is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes.

Queue limit

HYPERVAULT_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_LIMIT
notify_webhook queue_limit

Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

Client key Environment Variable MINIO_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_KEY Configuration Setting notify_webhook client_key Specify the path to the client private key to use for performing mTLS authentication to the webhook service. Comment Environment Variable MINIO_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_COMMENT Configuration Setting notify_webhook comment Specify a comment to associate with the Webhook configuration. Queue dir This value is deprecated. Environment Variable MINIO_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_DIR Configuration Setting notify_webhook queue_dir Specify the directory path to enable MinIO’s persistent event store for undelivered messages, such as /opt/minio/events. MinIO AIStor stores undelivered events in the specified store while the webhook service is offline and replays the stored events when connectivity resumes. Queue limit Environment Variable MINIO_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_LIMIT Configuration Setting notify_webhook queue_limit Specify the maximum limit for undelivered messages. Defaults to 100000.

title: Object Lambda Function Settings | HyperVault Documentation
html:
Object Lambda Function Settings

This page documents environment variables for configuring HyperVault to publish data to an HTTP webhook endpoint and trigger an Object Lambda function. See Transforms with Object Lambda for more complete documentation and tutorials on using these environment variables.

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier _ID for each set of related settings.

export HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_myfunction="on"
export HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_myfunction="https://webhook-1.example.net"
export HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_yourfunction="on"
export HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_yourfunction="https://webhook-2.example.net"

You can specify multiple targets by appending a unique identifier :ID to the configuration key.

mc admin config set lambda_webhook:primary enable="on" endpoint="https://webhook.example.net"

mc admin config set lambda_webhook:secondary enable="on" endpoint="https://webhook.example.net"
Each configuration setting controls fundamental HyperVault behavior and functionality. Test configuration changes in a lower environment, such as DEV or QA, before applying to production.

Enable

HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_ENABLE
lambda_webhook enable

Specify "on" to enable the Object Lambda webhook endpoint for a handler function.

Requires specifying HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT.

Endpoint

HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT
lambda_webhook endpoint

The HTTP endpoint of the lambda webhook for the handler function.

Auth token

HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_AUTH_TOKEN
lambda_webhook auth_token

Specify the opaque string or JWT authorization token to use for authenticating to the lambda webhook service.

HyperVault redacts this value when returned as part of mc admin config get.

Client cert

HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_CERT
lambda_webhook client_cert

Specify the path to the client certificate to use for performing mTLS authentication to the lambda webhook service.

Client key

HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_KEY
lambda_webhook client_key

Specify the path to the private key to use for performing mTLS authentication to the lambda webhook service.

Response header timeout

Optional

HYPERVAULT_LAMBDA_WEBHOOK_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT
lambda_webhook response_header_timeout

Specify the timeout period for receiving response headers from the lambda webhook server.

Specify a duration value, such as 120s or 2m.

Defaults to 0s (no timeout).

Requires HyperVault RELEASE.2025-08-29T21-27-49Z or later.
